<search query=""神" 老子 魏晋玄学 阮籍 《老子》注本 王弼 注疏发展" search_time="2026年5月19日12时26分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>NEO-TAOISM</title><hostname>Sci-Hub</hostname><url>https://sci-hub.se/downloads/2019-12-18/8e/19-neotaoism-1963.pdf#navpanes=0&view=FitH</url></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:2"><title>佛教為何能生根在中國</title><summary>*本文乃2005年1月9日，佛光大學生命研究所所長宋光宇教授在該校崇友人文講堂所主講的專題，《圓智天地》雙月刊第69期中曾登載全文。其後，宋教授應邀於天人實學研討會中發表專題演說，講題及其內容都與本文相當。編輯部得其授權，特於本期季刊中刊出本文，以饗讀者。</summary><hostname>天人研究總院</hostname><publisher>旋和季刊</publisher><author_list><author name="宋光宇" /><author name="张春美" /><author name="周雅容" /><author name="汪滿妹" /></author_list><url>https://academy.tienti.org/binder/res_049.pdf</url><publish_time>2009年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:3"><title>有邪？无邪？——王弼对《老子》之道的诠释</title><summary>欲言無邪？而物由以成。欲言有邪？而不見其形。無形無名者，萬物之宗也。——王弼《老子》十四章注《三國志·魏書·鍾會傳》卷二十八《注》引何劭〈王弼傳〉記載：弼幼而察慧，年十餘，好老氏，通辯能言。……時裴徽爲吏部郎，弼未弱冠，往造焉。徽一見而異之，問弼曰：「夫無者，誠萬物之所資也，然聖人莫肯致言，而老子申之無已者何？」弼曰：「聖人體无，无又不可以訓，故不說也。老子是有者也，故恆言無所不足。」¹裴徽提出的「問題」，主要在追問對於老子所謂的「無」的理解，如何與傳統（兩漢）以來儒家聖人顛撲不破的地位以及維繫現實名教秩序的規範取得協調，達至視域的融合。當時的何晏對於孔、老，儒、道之間的關係則有另一番理解，以爲老子的學說與聖人相「同」²。何晏的說法與王弼的立場本無不同，但直接了當的說同，並不能掩蓋實質的差異問題；相反的，承認傳統以來孔、老高下的定位說法，則讓王弼開啓了玄學會通孔、老，解決自然與名教關係課題的大門。本文送審過程，承蒙多位審查人分從不同角度提供實貴意見，謹致謝忱。¹〔晉〕陳壽撰，〔宋〕裴松之注：《三國志》（北京：中華書局，1995年），第3冊，頁795。²《世說新語·文學》十條「何晏注老子未畢」《注》引《文章敘錄》：「自儒者論以老子非聖人，絕禮棄學，晏說與聖人『同』，著論行於世也。」見楊勇：《世說新語校箋》（臺北：正文書局，1988年），頁153 - 154。下文稱引，隨文夾註，不標頁數。中國哲學的經典，構成了一個長遠的經典注疏傳統；大部分的哲學家，往往述而不作，信而好古。對西方人而言，覺得有趣的是，中國哲學的真理，往往不在於哲學家個人想表達什麼，而是他必須證明自己並沒有表達什麼。這就是中國哲學中的理解，正如高達美(Hans - Georg Gadamer)的詮釋學所言：「理解甚至根本不能被認爲是一種主體性的行爲，而要被認爲是一種置自身於傳統過程中的行動。」³所謂的真理，聖人之言、經典之言，作爲「被給與」的流傳物，它是跨越時空的，自古以固存，歷來許多優秀的哲學家總是要證明，他們所說的毫無新奇之處。這裏，王弼就是個典型的例子，依照王弼的理解，聖人體「無」而不言，從未表達什麼，這是不表達的能表達；老子是「有」，恆言不足，這是表達的不能表達。當然，玄學家們苦口婆心的訴說，表現在注疏經典之中的，在在表達，這些述而不作、古已有之的舊的東西（不表達），恰恰構成歷來哲學傳統之中的新的東西（表達）。《老子》第一章開宗明義指出：「道可道，非常道。名可名，非常名。」「無（名）」與「有（名）」二者，同出而異名，同謂之玄。此一同出於道的「兩者」——有與無、或有名與無名，在《帛書老子》則作：「兩者同出，異名同謂。」⁴作爲同出於道的兩個側面，或兩種不同的表達方式，玄之又玄，開啓了歷來老子哲</summary><hostname>中央研究院中国文哲研究所</hostname><publisher>中國文哲研究集刊 第二十九期</publisher><author_list><author name="周大興" /></author_list><url>https://www.litphil.sinica.edu.tw/bulletin/29/29-145-175.pdf</url><publish_time>2006年9月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:4"><title>王弼《老子注》的詮釋辨證Interpretative Dialectics of Wang Bi’s Exegesis of Lao-Tzu</title><summary>王弼是魏晋玄學最重要的思想家，也是中國哲學史上不世出的天才，他以二十四歲英年早逝，卻無礙於他的哲學成就：《周易注》被收入十三經注疏，《老子注》則成為通行本，影響後世深遠。歷來詮釋王弼思想的成果豐碩，精彩論點令人目不暇給，對於王弼思想的關注不限於華人社會，近期在中國出版，德國當代著名漢學家瓦格納(rudolf G. Wagner)《王弼〈老子注〉研究》就是海外漢學家長期關注王弼哲學的成果。本文針對海峽兩岸研究王弼卓然有成的林麗真、余敦康，以及歐陸的瓦格納等三人的王弼《老子注》的研究成果，歸納其進路、觀點，以及重大創穫。林麗真聚焦於王弼玄理的闡發，余敦康則提出通貫哲學與政治整體觀，著重王弼玄學的現實關懷，瓦格納則從語言哲學入手，提出「鍊體風格」的詮釋策略，豐富文本的內涵。台灣、大陸與歐洲學者對王弼的詮釋有共識，也有殊異，這樣的參照比較，不僅可以相互攻錯，擴大學術視野，也能進一步深化王弼思想、魏晉玄學的研究，極富學術意義。</summary><hostname>Semantic Scholar</hostname><publisher>Asian and African Studies XVI, 1 (2012), pp. 61–85</publisher><author_list><author name="蔡忠道" affiliation="台湾嘉义大学中文系" /></author_list><url>https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/f2b4/1b8e21aeb93da68804d8d64cbd10b5141a67.pdf</url><publish_time>2012年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:5"><title>论阮籍《咏怀》诗的创作</title><summary>阮籍《咏怀》，叙写的是生命的感思，具有强烈的思性色彩。阮籍《咏怀》诗的创作，表现出随意性、无目的性，发展了诗歌比兴的创作方法，而诗歌创作的这种变化，又与玄学思潮密切相关。</summary><hostname>维普</hostname><publisher>江西财经大学学报</publisher><author_list><author name="黄金明" affiliation="漳州师范学院 中文系" /></author_list><url>http://www.cqvip.com/QK/80754X/20033/7942937.html</url><publish_time>2003年5月15日0时0分</publish_time></document>
</search>

摘要
中文摘要
在老子《道德经》的注释史上,晋代王弼的《老子道德经注》是一部重要的解 经著作,但研究它的成果目前尚少｡王弼主要利用其抽象思辨与阐发义理探幽发微, 发展了老子的哲学思想;他凭着深厚的学养,开一代注风之先,以简驭繁､言约义 丰;不经意间对先秦至两汉以来的诸注家之风有较大破立｡王弼的义理之学对汉代 注疏之学进行了一次解释学上的革命,在经学的解读与研究上作出了重要贡献,他 的训诂特色是不可抹杀的｡本文旨在从内容上归纳王弼老注的训诂特色,并理清其 联系于语言哲学的问题,对其不足略陈陋见,充分发掘该书的训诂价值,从而引起 学界更广泛的关注｡
本文共分三章,第一章是王弼的生平及其《老子道德经注》,第二章阐述王弼 《老子道德经注》的训诂特色及语言哲学,第三章分析王弼《老子道德经注》的在 训诂史中的地位及其得失,最后得出结论｡
关键词:王弼,《老子道德经注》,
1
中文文摘
中文文摘
《道德经》是两千多年来中国文化的瑰宝,在中国传统文化发展史上,历代都 有一大批人对老子及其著作进行研究注释｡
先秦时代,就有人为《道德经》作注｡最早对老子研究颇有心得和见地的便是 韩非子｡韩非以才高而著世,他是法家的代表人物｡一般认为,先秦法家思想都源 于道家,因为尊道是立法的基础,法家也无一例外的倡导“因道制法”､“因道全 法”,“因道变化”｡因此,司马迁认为韩非归于黄老,他说韩非“喜刑名法术之 学,其归本于黄老"｡在《史记》编撰中,也将韩非与老子编在一起,设《老子韩 非列传》【¨ ,所表达的也是韩非深得老学真传之意｡
传统意义上的训诂学也发端于先秦时期,而兴盛于两汉｡魏晋时期训诂学处 于相对的低谷阶段,但这个时期的训诂仍沿着两汉高潮的余波发展,也有不少新的 成就｡除西汉的《河上公章句》外,三国时期魏国王弼的《老子注》对后世的影响 也非常大｡
魏晋时期,道家思想再次流行,当时三大显学是《老子》､《庄子》､《易经》, 《易经》中道家思想占了大半,因此,三大盛行玄学中,道家著作占了两个半｡笔 者认为所谓玄学的玄,无非是深､远､卓绝之意,恰如现代之所谓哲学是各门自然 学科和社会学科的概括总结,属于上层建筑领域的学问:即使在当时也属于高妙深 奥的显学! 真正懂得的人不多,精研绝学的人更少,就被蒙上唯心主义的“玄"的 外衣,实是一桩冤案;我们从《道德经》和王弼注本中看到更多的是自然界和人类 社会的辨证思想｡玄学人士可分为两类:一是在朝的,如何晏,王弼等;一是在野 的,如竹林七贤｡在众多注老作品中,当以王弼的注释影响最大｡王弼是三国魏时 的文学家,祖籍山东金乡人｡王弼对道学研究极深,他从本末､体用,动静､一多 等关系上来论证“以无为本”｡认识上提出“得意在忘象,得象在忘言”的思想｡ 以“凡有皆始于无”,肯定名教的“有”出于自然的“无"｡王弼研老注老的成果 十分丰富,作有《老子注》二卷､ 《老子略论》一卷､ 《老子指例略》二卷｡从这 些论著中我们不仅可以看到先哲们精深的哲思､智慧的灵光,还可以弥见语言哲学
【l 】司马迁著‘史记》卷六十三,岳麓书社1988年版第495页
I
福建师范大学硕士学位论文
对现实文学的启迪;无论从文本自身还是从文本解释学(阐释学或训诂学)来说都 可随处见其衍射｡
王力指出:“学习古代汉语最要紧的一个问题就是历史观点的问题｡’’i t l 孙帮 金在《魏晋南北朝时期的语言哲学》中有更切实的表述:“语言文字是随着时空条件 的转移而不断变化发展的,表现出明显的历史性与地域性特点｡历时性的语言固化 为文字,思想固化为经籍｡而作为经籍研究主干的经学在汉代如日中天的时代过去 之后,随即跌入低潮｡经典文本的神圣性遭到了人们的普遍质疑,在如何对待和阐 释经典文本的问题上涌现出不少新的观念;就阐释学的方法论而言,王弼的‘得意 忘言’论堪称魏晋南北朝时解释经典文本的主要范式｡’’【2】众所周知,文本注解主要 依赖于知性,强调的是客观性,而经典阐释则主要得力于悟性,它依赖的是创新的 勇气与能力,是智慧的彰显｡笔者赞同孙帮金对魏晋义理学的定论“在魏晋人们看 来,经典文本并不是僵死不变的教条,其本身说了什么并不重要,重要的是阐释者 透过文本而与自身的经验和理性相契合､相贯通｡因此,经典文本不仅应向历史开 放,也应该向当前(主体经验)开放;对文本的阐释与其说是一种还原,不如说是一 种创造｡这就是说,经典具有历史性的同时,还更应具有时代性,创造性｡这样一 来,魏晋义理之学对汉代注疏之学进行了一次解释学上的革命｡”【3】我们回顾历史, 哲学思想放射出夺目光华的两个时代都是历史上最动荡､政治上最混乱,社会上最 痛苦的时代,然而却是文化上､精神上相对独立､自由解放､富于智慧和热情的时 代(战国时代和魏晋时代),这是文化的幸运｡
魏晋玄学(我们不妨称之为与老子一脉相承的中国哲学)之所以发达就在于它 所探索的中心就是对社会的主体—人的终极关怀,即对精神,人格的本体研究;魏 晋士人具有很强的生命自省认识｡这种精神和思想的表达主要集中在论辩上(rE即 所谓清谈)因为论辩首先是一种群体行为,它要有许多人参加;其次,论辩又给个 人提供展示才情的机会,他们或辩论人格理想､或谈政治哲学,或直白反对名教礼 法｡这些玄思都具有鲜明的时代性｡
本文拟从训诂学的角度,着意介绍和归纳王弼《道德经》注的训诂特色及其体 现出的语言哲学,并对其不足略陈陋见,充分发掘该书的语言学价值,从而引起学 界更广泛的关注｡经学训诂的兴盛始于东汉,训诂范围逐渐从注经而扩大到注史､

IV

子､集｡史注新生了裴松之的《三国志注》､韦昭的《国语解》,经注有王弼,韩 康伯的《周易注》､何晏《论语集解》､皇侃的《论语义疏》,杜预《春秋经传 集解》､郭璞《山海经注》和《尔雅注》,范宁的《春秋毂梁传集解》｡其中《论语 集解》价值很大,皇侃就是依据它编著了《论语义疏》,其行文不但解释词义､ 串讲旬义,还阐发章旨,总括全篇大义｡《易经》注本以魏王弼､韩康伯影响至 深,这是经典注释由单一析词解字向义理阐发的重要标志,这一历史契机缘于东汉 后期政治局势的急剧动荡和社会环境的普遍恶化而导致官方文化专制下的儒学独尊 地位的逐渐动摇,训诂实践范围的拓展使得训诂学有了摆脱经学附庸地位的可 能性:至汉末,三国之际,以《易》､ 《老》, 《庄》为研究对象,以清谈名理为 标志,糅合了儒､释,道三家学说的玄学就应运而生｡反映到注解上就是,许多魏 晋人著书不再仅仅注意字词方面的单向训诂了,而常常立体式,多方向发挥,阐发 义理｡王弼注《老子》,郭象注《庄子》就是这样的代表｡
本文认为王弼注《易》《老》,绝不仅仅是为了撰之同好,藏之名山｡形而上的 玄学蕴含着丰富的政治哲学,哲学是政治的先导,政治是为现实服务的｡嵇康就因 为玄学思想而死,他“越名教而任自然,非汤武而薄周孔”【l 】,其政治理想是“不 以天下私亲,宁济四海蒸民’’【2J否定了“宰割天下以奉其私"的罪恶统治;这支带 刺的玫瑰自然得不到司马昭的青睐! 研究王弼的《老》注,本文首先从其文本的解 释策略和文本修辞入手,这可以从解经思路中得到启发:他在《周易略例· 明彖》 中说:“物无妄然,必有其理”､“品制万变,宗主存焉”【3】,即找准释经的主线｡ 哲学上的认识论必然会在语言学上有所体现和应用,具体而言就是凸现了“崇本息 末”这条主线,抓关键,抓中心环节｡明白了《老子》经中蕴含的喻象系统,就明 白了“道生万物”的主线｡其次,在解说技巧层面,王弼通过置换关键词,介入主 语,解释比拟､明喻､隐喻,转喻,释句,通译等手段达到准确界定概念,约减语 词多义性､统一注本与经文内在思想逻辑的目的｡其三,象语言思维的运用｡王弼 在《易》注中推断先圣们曾有观象系辞的规则,认为“意以象尽,象以言著”,“得 意忘象"的语言思维使他在文笔和哲思上与老子遥相辉映,一道同风｡在篇章修辞 上有着同构的性质,在句式上多采用链式结构,为后来的骈体文风奠定了基础｡

王弼《老子道德经注》研究

摘要
中文摘要
在老子《道德经》的注释史上,晋代王弼的《老子道德经注》是一部重要的解 经著作,但研究它的成果目前尚少｡王弼主要利用其抽象思辨与阐发义理探幽发微, 发展了老子的哲学思想;他凭着深厚的学养,开一代注风之先,以简驭繁､言约义 丰;不经意间对先秦至两汉以来的诸注家之风有较大破立｡王弼的义理之学对汉代 注疏之学进行了一次解释学上的革命,在经学的解读与研究上作出了重要贡献,他 的训诂特色是不可抹杀的｡本文旨在从内容上归纳王弼老注的训诂特色,并理清其 联系于语言哲学的问题,对其不足略陈陋见,充分发掘该书的训诂价值,从而引起 学界更广泛的关注｡
本文共分三章,第一章是王弼的生平及其《老子道德经注》,第二章阐述王弼 《老子道德经注》的训诂特色及语言哲学,第三章分析王弼《老子道德经注》的在 训诂史中的地位及其得失,最后得出结论｡

中文文摘
《道德经》是两千多年来中国文化的瑰宝,在中国传统文化发展史上,历代都 有一大批人对老子及其著作进行研究注释｡
先秦时代,就有人为《道德经》作注｡最早对老子研究颇有心得和见地的便是 韩非子｡韩非以才高而著世,他是法家的代表人物｡一般认为,先秦法家思想都源 于道家,因为尊道是立法的基础,法家也无一例外的倡导“因道制法”､“因道全 法”,“因道变化”｡因此,司马迁认为韩非归于黄老,他说韩非“喜刑名法术之 学,其归本于黄老"｡在《史记》编撰中,也将韩非与老子编在一起,设《老子韩 非列传》【¨ ,所表达的也是韩非深得老学真传之意｡
传统意义上的训诂学也发端于先秦时期,而兴盛于两汉｡魏晋时期训诂学处 于相对的低谷阶段,但这个时期的训诂仍沿着两汉高潮的余波发展,也有不少新的 成就｡除西汉的《河上公章句》外,三国时期魏国王弼的《老子注》对后世的影响 也非常大｡
魏晋时期,道家思想再次流行,当时三大显学是《老子》､《庄子》､《易经》, 《易经》中道家思想占了大半,因此,三大盛行玄学中,道家著作占了两个半｡笔 者认为所谓玄学的玄,无非是深､远､卓绝之意,恰如现代之所谓哲学是各门自然 学科和社会学科的概括总结,属于上层建筑领域的学问:即使在当时也属于高妙深 奥的显学! 真正懂得的人不多,精研绝学的人更少,就被蒙上唯心主义的“玄"的 外衣,实是一桩冤案;我们从《道德经》和王弼注本中看到更多的是自然界和人类 社会的辨证思想｡玄学人士可分为两类:一是在朝的,如何晏,王弼等;一是在野 的,如竹林七贤｡在众多注老作品中,当以王弼的注释影响最大｡王弼是三国魏时 的文学家,祖籍山东金乡人｡王弼对道学研究极深,他从本末､体用,动静､一多 等关系上来论证“以无为本”｡认识上提出“得意在忘象,得象在忘言”的思想｡ 以“凡有皆始于无”,肯定名教的“有”出于自然的“无"｡王弼研老注老的成果 十分丰富,作有《老子注》二卷､ 《老子略论》一卷､ 《老子指例略》二卷｡从这 些论著中我们不仅可以看到先哲们精深的哲思､智慧的灵光,还可以弥见语言哲学

对现实文学的启迪;无论从文本自身还是从文本解释学(阐释学或训诂学)来说都 可随处见其衍射｡
王力指出:“学习古代汉语最要紧的一个问题就是历史观点的问题｡’’i t l 孙帮 金在《魏晋南北朝时期的语言哲学》中有更切实的表述:“语言文字是随着时空条件 的转移而不断变化发展的,表现出明显的历史性与地域性特点｡历时性的语言固化 为文字,思想固化为经籍｡而作为经籍研究主干的经学在汉代如日中天的时代过去 之后,随即跌入低潮｡经典文本的神圣性遭到了人们的普遍质疑,在如何对待和阐 释经典文本的问题上涌现出不少新的观念;就阐释学的方法论而言,王弼的‘得意 忘言’论堪称魏晋南北朝时解释经典文本的主要范式｡’’【2】众所周知,文本注解主要 依赖于知性,强调的是客观性,而经典阐释则主要得力于悟性,它依赖的是创新的 勇气与能力,是智慧的彰显｡笔者赞同孙帮金对魏晋义理学的定论“在魏晋人们看 来,经典文本并不是僵死不变的教条,其本身说了什么并不重要,重要的是阐释者 透过文本而与自身的经验和理性相契合､相贯通｡因此,经典文本不仅应向历史开 放,也应该向当前(主体经验)开放;对文本的阐释与其说是一种还原,不如说是一 种创造｡这就是说,经典具有历史性的同时,还更应具有时代性,创造性｡这样一 来,魏晋义理之学对汉代注疏之学进行了一次解释学上的革命｡”【3】我们回顾历史, 哲学思想放射出夺目光华的两个时代都是历史上最动荡､政治上最混乱,社会上最 痛苦的时代,然而却是文化上､精神上相对独立､自由解放､富于智慧和热情的时 代(战国时代和魏晋时代),这是文化的幸运｡
魏晋玄学(我们不妨称之为与老子一脉相承的中国哲学)之所以发达就在于它 所探索的中心就是对社会的主体—人的终极关怀,即对精神,人格的本体研究;魏 晋士人具有很强的生命自省认识｡这种精神和思想的表达主要集中在论辩上(rE即 所谓清谈)因为论辩首先是一种群体行为,它要有许多人参加;其次,论辩又给个 人提供展示才情的机会,他们或辩论人格理想､或谈政治哲学,或直白反对名教礼 法｡这些玄思都具有鲜明的时代性｡
本文拟从训诂学的角度,着意介绍和归纳王弼《道德经》注的训诂特色及其体 现出的语言哲学,并对其不足略陈陋见,充分发掘该书的语言学价值,从而引起学 界更广泛的关注｡经学训诂的兴盛始于东汉,训诂范围逐渐从注经而扩大到注史､

子､集｡史注新生了裴松之的《三国志注》､韦昭的《国语解》,经注有王弼,韩 康伯的《周易注》､何晏《论语集解》､皇侃的《论语义疏》,杜预《春秋经传 集解》､郭璞《山海经注》和《尔雅注》,范宁的《春秋毂梁传集解》｡其中《论语 集解》价值很大,皇侃就是依据它编著了《论语义疏》,其行文不但解释词义､ 串讲旬义,还阐发章旨,总括全篇大义｡《易经》注本以魏王弼､韩康伯影响至 深,这是经典注释由单一析词解字向义理阐发的重要标志,这一历史契机缘于东汉 后期政治局势的急剧动荡和社会环境的普遍恶化而导致官方文化专制下的儒学独尊 地位的逐渐动摇,训诂实践范围的拓展使得训诂学有了摆脱经学附庸地位的可 能性:至汉末,三国之际,以《易》､ 《老》, 《庄》为研究对象,以清谈名理为 标志,糅合了儒､释,道三家学说的玄学就应运而生｡反映到注解上就是,许多魏 晋人著书不再仅仅注意字词方面的单向训诂了,而常常立体式,多方向发挥,阐发 义理｡王弼注《老子》,郭象注《庄子》就是这样的代表｡
本文认为王弼注《易》《老》,绝不仅仅是为了撰之同好,藏之名山｡形而上的 玄学蕴含着丰富的政治哲学,哲学是政治的先导,政治是为现实服务的｡嵇康就因 为玄学思想而死,他“越名教而任自然,非汤武而薄周孔”【l 】,其政治理想是“不 以天下私亲,宁济四海蒸民’’【2J否定了“宰割天下以奉其私"的罪恶统治;这支带 刺的玫瑰自然得不到司马昭的青睐! 研究王弼的《老》注,本文首先从其文本的解 释策略和文本修辞入手,这可以从解经思路中得到启发:他在《周易略例· 明彖》 中说:“物无妄然,必有其理”､“品制万变,宗主存焉”【3】,即找准释经的主线｡ 哲学上的认识论必然会在语言学上有所体现和应用,具体而言就是凸现了“崇本息 末”这条主线,抓关键,抓中心环节｡明白了《老子》经中蕴含的喻象系统,就明 白了“道生万物”的主线｡其次,在解说技巧层面,王弼通过置换关键词,介入主 语,解释比拟､明喻､隐喻,转喻,释句,通译等手段达到准确界定概念,约减语 词多义性､统一注本与经文内在思想逻辑的目的｡其三,象语言思维的运用｡王弼 在《易》注中推断先圣们曾有观象系辞的规则,认为“意以象尽,象以言著”,“得 意忘象"的语言思维使他在文笔和哲思上与老子遥相辉映,一道同风｡在篇章修辞 上有着同构的性质,在句式上多采用链式结构,为后来的骈体文风奠定了基础｡

As nearly everyone who has any familiarity with the text will recognize, this is a variation from the line as it is now known from the Lao tzu text itself, where we have 無名天地之始 'the nameless, the beginning of Heaven and Earth', and the Shih chi has been looked upon as the purveyor of sloppy and careless scholarship for nearly two millennia.¹ With the discovery about ten years ago of the Ma wang tui (milledenniA MWT) silk manuscripts of the Lao tzu dating from around 200 B.C. we are able to see that this Shih chi rendering of the line was neither sloppy nor careless, because in fact it matches in its essential features the MWT version, both the A and B manuscripts of which have 無名萬物之始也.² Given the evidence of the MWT MSS coupled with the Shih chi form of the line we are inclined to suppose that this was the prevalent Han version of the text, and that the form with the 天地 instead of 萬物 is a later innovation. <answer>## Executive summary

This report synthesizes evidence on how to support children’s and adolescents’ healthy development by balancing schoolwork, rest, and interests, and by helping them discover meaningful goals. It draws on educational psychology, child development, and time-management research to provide practical, data-driven recommendations for families and educators<cite id="12">Time management and prioritization of schoolwork</cite><cite id="13">Leisure and psychological needs in adolescents</cite><cite id="18">Self-determination theory and intrinsic motivation</cite><cite id="19">Developmental neuroscience and executive function</cite>.

## Why balance matters for development

Neuroscience shows that adolescents’ prefrontal cortex is still maturing, which means they benefit from structured routines that include focused study, adequate sleep, and regular physical activity to support attention and emotional regulation<cite id="19">Prefrontal cortex development and its implications</cite>. In this context, balancing schoolwork with rest and hobbies is not optional—it is essential for maintaining cognitive and emotional health<cite id="12">Prioritizing schoolwork and scheduling rest</cite>.

## How to balance schoolwork, rest, and hobbies

A practical approach is to start with schoolwork as the foundation and then build in time for hobbies and rest around it. Teens should choose activities they genuinely enjoy, avoid overcommitment, and learn to say no when necessary<cite id="12">Prioritize schoolwork and choose enjoyable activities</cite>. Creating a weekly schedule that blocks out study, activity, and free time helps visualize where to fit things and where overcommitment may occur<cite id="12">Use a planner and block time</cite>.

Evidence-based time-management strategies include the Eisenhower Matrix to prioritize tasks and the Pomodoro Technique (25 minutes focused work, 5 minutes break) to sustain concentration and reduce burnout<cite id="16">SMART goals, Eisenhower Matrix, and Pomodoro</cite>. A commonly recommended rule is to limit hobby time to about 30% of total discretionary time, with flexibility to adjust during high-pressure periods such as exams<cite id="12">30% time rule and dynamic adjustment</cite>.

## Choosing and nurturing interests

Leisure activities can significantly enhance well-being when they satisfy basic psychological needs—competence, autonomy, and relatedness<cite id="13">Need satisfaction in leisure and life satisfaction</cite>. Autonomy-supportive parenting encourages youth to pursue interests that align with their values, which in turn promotes intrinsic motivation and long-term happiness<cite id="18">Autonomy-support and intrinsic goals</cite>. Selecting hobbies that complement schoolwork (e.g., science-related projects for a physics enthusiast) can create synergies that boost both academic performance and personal satisfaction<cite id="12">Complementary and long-term-value interests</cite>.

## Supporting goal discovery and direction

Self-determination theory emphasizes that goals pursued for their own sake—such as community involvement—are more strongly linked to well-being than extrinsic goals like wealth or status<cite id="18">Intrinsic vs. extrinsic goals and well-being</cite>. Helping teens explore interests and reflect on what matters to them can clarify intrinsic motivations and guide meaningful life directions<cite id="18">Encouraging intrinsic life goals</cite>.

## Practical recommendations

- Prioritize schoolwork and schedule rest and hobbies around it, using planners or apps to block time<cite id="12">Schedule commitments and leave gaps</cite>.
- Choose activities that genuinely interest the child and align with their strengths and values<cite id="12">Choose enjoyable and complementary activities</cite>.
- Apply time-management techniques such as SMART goal-setting, the Eisenhower Matrix, and the Pomodoro Technique to stay organized and focused<cite id="16">Goal-setting and time-management tools</cite>.
- Limit hobby time to about 30% of discretionary hours and adjust during exams or busy periods<cite id="12">Time allocation and dynamic adjustment</cite>.
- Encourage autonomy in interest selection and provide support without forcing choices<cite id="18">Autonomy-support and intrinsic motivation</cite>.
- Reflect regularly on what brings joy and meaning to help identify long-term goals<cite id="18">Intrinsic goals and well-being</cite>.

## Evidence base

Research on adolescent leisure shows that activities that satisfy competence and relatedness needs are strongly associated with life satisfaction<cite id="13">Competence and relatedness in leisure</cite>. Educational psychology provides tested time-management frameworks that help teens balance demands<cite id="16">Productivity and organization strategies</cite>. Developmental neuroscience underscores the importance of routines and rest for cognitive development during adolescence<cite id="19">Brain development and routine needs</cite>.

## Conclusion

A healthy balance of schoolwork, rest, and interests supports both academic success and emotional well-being. By using evidence-based time-management practices, encouraging autonomy in hobby selection, and reflecting on intrinsic motivations, families and educators can help children develop the skills to thrive<cite id="12">Balancing school and personal life</cite><cite id="16">Goal-setting and organization</cite><cite id="18">Intrinsic motivation and well-being</cite>.</answer>

Are you feeling overwhelmed trying to juggle your studies with sports practice, music lessons, or other activities? You’re not alone. While extracurricular activities are great for making friends and developing new skills, it can be tricky to find the right balance between these activities and your academic ones. Let’s explore some practical ways you can manage your time and energy effectively.

## Why are extracurricular activities important?

While keeping up with your studies is important of course, activities outside the classroom can add so much value to your high school experience too. Being involved in extracurricular activities can:

- Help you discover new interests and talents

- Build valuable skills for your future

- Look great on job and university applications

- Provide a fun break from studying

- Help you make new friends

But it’s important to find the right balance so that neither your grades nor your activities suffer.

## Tips for balancing academic and extracurricular activities

The key to balancing academic and extracurricular activities is smart time management, so here are our top tips for making it work.

### Start with your studies

This might not come as a surprise, but your school work should be your foundation. Make sure things like assignments and exams have top priority – then, you can plan your other activities around them.

### Choose activities you truly enjoy

Try and avoid joining clubs or doing certain activities just because they’ll look good on your resume. Pick things that actually interest you – you’ll be more motivated to make time for them, get more out of the experience, and just enjoy yourself more too.

### Be realistic about your commitments

Like it or not, there are only so many hours in each day. So if you want to add more activities to your calendar, consider:

- How many hours per week each activity requires

- Travel time to and from activities

- Whether activities clash with other commitments

- Busy periods at school (like exam time)

- Time off to rest and recharge

### Learn to prioritise

You don’t have to do everything! It’s better to fully commit to a few activities than to spread yourself too thin across many. And if you’re feeling overwhelmed, it’s totally okay to step back from some commitments – your health and wellbeing always comes first.

## Creating a schedule that works

Having a clear schedule is one of the best ways to make sure you can fit everything in without getting stressed. Here’s a simple way to put together a calendar to keep track of your commitments:

### Use a planner

Writing everything down is a great way to help you stay on track each day. There are <link reference_id="<|superscript|>:17-<|link|>:2" text="some great planning apps out there" /> to help you put your schedule together, but good old-fashioned pen and paper does the trick just as well.

### List all your commitments

Whatever method you use, your first step is to work out what all your commitments are and how long they take. Include things like:

- Class times

- Assignment and exam dates

- Activity schedules

- Study periods

- Free time

### Block out your time

Once you know what you’re doing, you just need to work out when to do it! In your planner, allocate specific times each day or week for each activity and commitment.

If you find some of them overlap or you don’t have enough time in your week for all of them, go back and work out what should take top priority, and schedule it first.

如何引导青少年正确处理学业与兴趣爱好的平衡模式

一、引言 青少年时期是个人成长的关键阶段，学业与兴趣爱好的平衡直接关系到学生的全面发展、心理健康及未来竞争力。科学地引导青少年处理二者关系，不仅能提升学习效率，还能培养综合素质。本文将从青少年心理特点、平衡原则、具体方法及家长和学校的作用等方面，探讨如何帮助青少年建立合理的平衡模式。 二、青少年心理特点与平衡原则 （一）青少年心理特点 1. 自我意识增强：青少年开始关注个人兴趣，但容易因学业压力产生选择困难。 2. 注意力易分散：兴趣爱好的吸引力可能导致学习分心，反之学业压力也可能影响兴趣投入。 3. 可塑性强：通过正确引导，能够形成受益终生的时间管理习惯。 （二）平衡原则 1. \*\*学业优先原则\*\*：确保基础学业不受兴趣影响，尤其在高中学业压力阶段。 2. \*\*适度发展原则\*\*：兴趣投入时间不宜超过总时间的30%，避免过度沉迷。 3. \*\*动态调整原则\*\*：根据学业阶段和个人需求灵活调整比例，如考前减少兴趣时间。 三、建立平衡模式的具体方法 （一）时间管理技巧 1. 制定计划表： (1) 每日固定分配：如学习6小时，兴趣2小时，休息2小时。 (2) 学期目标分解：将大项目（如学科竞赛或艺术创作）与学习任务穿插安排。 2. 使用工具辅助： (1) 番茄工作法：25分钟专注学习，5分钟兴趣短暂放松。 (2) 日历标记法：用不同颜色标注学业和兴趣活动时段。 （二）兴趣选择与投入策略 1. 兴趣筛选标准： (1) 与学业互补：如物理爱好者可尝试机器人制作。 (2) 具备长期价值：如阅读、运动等能提升综合素质。 2. 逐步投入原则： (1) 初期短时尝试：每周1小时接触新兴趣，确认可行性。 (2) 逐步增加时长：若效果显著，可每月递增30分钟。 （三）解决冲突的应对方法 1. 优先级排序： (1) 临近考试时：暂停高耗能兴趣（如竞技体育），保留低强度爱好（如绘画）。 (2) 学业任务繁重时：减少兴趣的社交属性（如团队运动），改为个人项目（如乐器练习）。 2. 寻求支持： (1) 与教师沟通：争取弹性作业时间。 (2) 家长协助：共同规划周末时间分配。 四、家长与学校的引导作用 （一）家长的角色 1. 树立榜样：家长自身需平衡工作与休闲。 2. 避免强制：兴趣选择应以鼓励为主，避免因成绩否定爱好。 3. 提供资源：如报名兴趣班、购买器材等。 （二）学校的支持措施 1. 开设选修课：如编程、戏剧等满足多元需求。 2. 组织活动：通过社团、兴趣小组促进平衡发展。 3. 心理辅导：设立咨询室帮助解决时间管理难题。 五、结论 青少年学业与兴趣的平衡需要科学规划、动态调整及多方支持。通过合理的时间管理、兴趣筛选和冲突解决策略，结合家长与学校的配合，能够培养出既专注学业又富有个性的个体。关键在于建立“学业是基础，兴趣是调剂”的认知，让成长过程更健康、高效。 一、引言 青少年时期是个人成长的关键阶段，学业与兴趣爱好的平衡直接关系到学生的全面发展、心理健康及未来竞争力。科学地引导青少年处理二者关系，不仅能提升学习效率，还能培养综合素质。本文将从青少年心理特点、平衡原则、具体方法及家长和学校的作用等方面，探讨如何帮助青少年建立合理的平衡模式。 二、青少年心理特点与平衡原则 （一）青少年心理特点 1. 自我意识增强：青少年开始关注个人兴趣，渴望通过爱好展现独特性和价值感，但同时也容易因学业压力产生选择困难，尤其是在面临升学或未来规划时，更难抉择。这种内在的矛盾可能导致焦虑或时间浪费在犹豫不决中。 2. 注意力易分散：青少年大脑前额叶皮层尚未完全发育成熟，导致注意力容易受到外界刺激的干扰。兴趣爱好的吸引力（如游戏、音乐、运动）可能导致学习分心，反之，繁重的学业压力也可能让青少年将精力转移到兴趣上以寻求放松，从而影响学习投入。 3. 可塑性强：青少年正处于习惯养成的重要时期，通过正确引导，能够形成受益终生的时间管理习惯和平衡生活的能力。这一阶段的教育和引导对未来的生活模式有深远影响。 （二）平衡原则 1. \*\*学业优先原则\*\*：在青少年阶段，特别是中学阶段，学业是奠定未来基础的核心任务。必须确保基础学业不受兴趣爱好的过度影响，保证有足够的时间和精力投入到系统学习和知识掌握上。这意味着在安排兴趣时间时，不能以牺牲必要的睡眠、学习和复习时间为代价。例如，高中生可以设定每天至少保证6-8小时的有效学习时间，周末也要有固定的复习和预习安排。 2. \*\*适度发展原则\*\*：兴趣爱好的投入时间不宜超过总可支配时间的30%-40%。具体比例需要根据学生的年级、学业压力、兴趣类型和个人精力状况灵活调整，但应避免过度沉迷。例如，一个高中生在周末，如果总的可支配时间（除去睡眠、基本生活必需时间）是20小时，那么兴趣爱好的投入时间建议控制在6-8小时以内。过高的投入可能导致精力透支，反而影响学业和身心健康。 3. \*\*动态调整原则\*\*：平衡模式不是一成不变的，需要根据学业阶段、个人需求、兴趣发展情况以及外部环境的变化进行灵活调整。例如，在学期初或面临重要考试前，可以适当减少兴趣爱好的投入时间，增加学习时间；在假期或学业任务较轻的阶段，可以增加兴趣爱好的时间。这种动态调整能力本身也是一种重要的生存技能。 三、建立平衡模式的具体方法 （一）时间管理技巧 1. 制定计划表： (1) 每日固定分配：根据每日的生物钟和个人习惯，制定详细的时间表。例如，早上7点起床，晚上10点睡觉，中间安排三餐、学习、兴趣和休息时间。学习时段可以细化到具体科目，兴趣时间可以分配给特定的爱好，如周一、三下午练习乐器，周五晚上进行体育活动。确保计划表留有弹性，如每天安排15-30分钟的缓冲时间应对突发状况。 (2) 学期目标分解：将学期或学年的大目标（如提高某科成绩到90分、完成一个艺术项目、达到某个运动水平）分解为每周、每天的小任务。将这些小任务纳入每日计划表，确保在追求兴趣的同时，不偏离学业大方向。例如，计划学期末提高数学成绩，可以在每日计划表中安排每天15分钟的专项练习时间。 2. 使用工具辅助： (1) 番茄工作法：将学习或兴趣活动分解为25分钟专注工作（Pomodoro）和5分钟短暂休息的循环。25分钟内完全投入，期间关闭手机通知、社交媒体等干扰源；5分钟休息时可以站起来走动、喝水、看看窗外，让大脑放松。每完成4个Pomodoro后，进行一次较长的休息（15-30分钟）。这种方法有助于提高专注度，并让兴趣爱好的投入也更具效率。 (2) 日历标记法：使用实体日历或电子日历（如日历应用），用不同颜色标记不同类型的活动时段：红色代表学习、黄色代表兴趣、绿色代表休息、蓝色代表社交等。视觉化的时间分配有助于直观了解时间使用情况，并更容易遵守计划。可以每周初打印或更新日历，放在显眼位置。 （二）兴趣选择与投入策略 1. 兴趣筛选标准： (1) 与学业互补：选择能够与学业知识产生关联的兴趣爱好，可以相辅相成。例如，喜欢物理的学生可以尝试参与机器人制作或科学实验社团；对历史感兴趣的学生可以通过阅读、制作模型来加深理解。这种互补性不仅能让兴趣更有深度，也能反过来促进学业。 (2) 具备长期价值：优先选择那些能够培养持久能力、提升综合素质的兴趣，如阅读、乐器、体育运动、编程、艺术创作等。这些爱好不仅能带来乐趣，还能锻炼思维能力、毅力、协作能力等，对个人长远发展更有益。应避免选择那些短期刺激但长期价值不大的兴趣，如过度沉迷某些游戏。 2. 逐步投入原则： (1) 初期短时尝试：对于新发现的兴趣，应先进行短时间的尝试，以评估自己的兴趣程度和承受能力。每周安排1小时或每次30分钟接触新兴趣，如报名一个周末短期体验班、借阅相关书籍或观看教学视频。观察自己是否享受这个过程，是否愿意持续投入。 (2) The aim was to identify the extent to which satisfaction of the three needs explained the relationship between participation in leisure activities and life satisfaction. These proposed mechanisms were based on previous empirical work and the theoretical frameworks of self-determination theory, and were tested in a nationally representative sample of Norwegian adolescents (N = 3,273) aged 15 and 16 years (51.8 % boys). The structural equation analysis showed that competence and relatedness satisfaction fully mediated the association between participation in activities and life satisfaction. Autonomy satisfaction had a direct positive effect on life satisfaction but did not show any mediation effect. The positive processes of psychological need satisfaction, and especially the need for competence and relatedness, experienced in the leisure activity domain thus seem to be beneficial for adolescents’ well-being. These findings add to previous research investigating the positive impact of need satisfaction in other important domains in the lives of children and adolescents.</summary><hostname>Europe PMC</hostname><publisher>J Youth Adolescence</publisher><author_list><author name="Ingrid Leversen" affiliation="Department of Health Promotion and Development, Faculty of Psychology, University of Bergen, P.O. problem: 我今年五十三岁，体重一百六十斤，为我提供一份两周的食谱，包含更科学、健康、简单易做的营养搭配（我是中国人）
final_response:
<answer>根据您的年龄和体重，BMI约为26.5，属于超重范围，建议采用国家卫健委《成人肥胖食养指南（2024年版）》推荐的限能量平衡膳食，每日能量摄入男性约1200～1500kcal、女性约1000～1200kcal，三大宏量营养素供能比为脂肪20%～30%、蛋白质15%～20%、碳水化合物50%～60%，早中晚三餐供能比3:4:3，并注意定时定量、细嚼慢咽、蔬菜先于主食的进餐顺序<cite id="11">健康减肥该怎么吃？推荐每日能量摄入男性1200～1500kcal、女性1000～1200kcal，三大宏量营养素供能比及早中晚三餐供能比，定时定量规律进餐，细嚼慢咽，改变进餐顺序</cite>。考虑到您为中年女性，建议每日能量控制在约1200kcal左右，以实现适度能量负平衡，同时保障营养密度<cite id="11">控制总能量摄入，推荐每日能量摄入男性1200～1500kcal、女性1000～1200kcal</cite>。

主食应以全谷物和杂豆类为主，替代约1/2的精白米面，有助于增加膳食纤维和体积感，延长饱腹时间；蔬菜每日至少500g，深色蔬菜占一半以上，可选择绿叶菜、瓜茄类、菌菇类等多样化食材，避免单一；水果优先选择低GI种类（如柚子、草莓、蓝莓、猕猴桃），每日200～350g，最好在两餐之间食用，避免高糖水果过量摄入<cite id="11">鼓励主食以全谷物为主，适当增加粗粮并减少精白米面摄入；可选择绿叶菜、瓜茄类、菌菇类等多种蔬菜，避免单一</cite><cite id="3">水果含糖量较高，过量摄入会导致热量超标，建议每日摄入量200-350g，优先选低GI水果（柚子、草莓、蓝莓、猕猴桃），最好在两餐之间食用</cite>。蛋白质应优质优先，每日1.0～1.2g/kg体重，可选择鱼虾、去皮鸡/鸭胸、瘦牛/猪肉、鸡蛋、无糖酸奶、豆腐等低脂高蛋白食物，以维持肌肉质量并增加饱腹感<cite id="11">优先选择脂肪含量低的食材，如瘦肉、去皮鸡胸肉、鱼虾等；优先选择低脂或脱脂奶类</cite><cite id="5">蛋白：鱼虾、去皮鸡/鸭胸、瘦牛/猪、鸡蛋、豆腐、无糖酸奶</cite>。

烹饪油每日不超过20～25g，食盐不超过5g，添加糖最好控制在25g以下，严格限制饮酒，避免高能量食物（如油炸食品、含糖烘焙糕点、糖果、肥肉等）<cite id="11">每天食盐摄入量不超过5g，烹调油不超过20～25g，添加糖的摄入量最好控制在25g以下，严格限制饮酒；少吃油炸食品、含糖烘焙糕点、糖果、肥肉等高能量食物</cite>。此外，每周应安排中低强度有氧运动5～7天，每次至少10～20分钟，抗阻运动2～3天，隔天1次，以促进脂肪代谢并保留肌肉质量<cite id="11">减重的运动原则是中低强度有氧运动为主，抗阻运动为辅，有氧运动每周5～7天，至少隔天1次，抗阻运动每周2～3天，隔天1次，每次10～20分钟</cite>。

以下是一份两周食谱示例，采用“蔬菜—蛋白质—主食”的进餐顺序，每餐热量控制在约300～400kcal，全天约1200kcal（可根据实际食量微调）<cite id="11">推荐早中晚三餐供能比为3：4：3；改变进餐顺序为“蔬菜一肉类一主食”有助于减少高能量食物的进食量</cite>：

**第一周**
- 早餐（约300kcal）：1个水煮蛋 + 1小碗燕麦粥（约30g燕麦） + 1个拳头大小苹果 + 1杯无糖豆浆（约200ml）<cite id="5">主食推荐燕麦、全麦等全谷物；蛋白推荐鸡蛋、无糖酸奶；水果推荐苹果等低GI水果</cite>
- 上午加餐（约100kcal）：无糖酸奶100g + 蓝莓一把（约50g）<cite id="2">上午加餐推荐无糖酸奶+蓝莓</cite>
- 午餐（约450kcal）：杂粮饭1小碗（约120g，含糙米、小米等） + 清蒸鱼（如鲈鱼）100g + 清炒西兰花200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">主食推荐全谷物；蛋白推荐鱼虾；蔬菜推荐绿叶菜、瓜茄类</cite><cite id="2">午餐示例含杂粮饭+鱼+西兰花</cite>
- 下午加餐（约100kcal）：圣女果5～6颗 + 原味坚果5颗（如巴旦木）<cite id="2">水果可选圣女果；坚果适量</cite>
- 晚餐（约350kcal）：蒸南瓜1小碗（约150g） + 香煎鸡胸肉100g + 蒜蓉空心菜200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">主食可选南瓜等根茎类；蛋白推荐鸡胸肉</cite><cite id="2">晚餐示例含南瓜+鸡胸肉+空心菜</cite>

- 早餐（约300kcal）：1个水煮蛋 + 全麦面包1片 + 1小碗玉米糊（约30g玉米） + 1个拳头大小橙子 + 1杯无糖豆浆（约200ml）<cite id="5">全谷物推荐玉米、全麦；水果推荐橙子</cite>
- 上午加餐（约100kcal）：无糖酸奶100g + 草莓5～6颗<cite id="3">低GI水果推荐草莓</cite>
- 午餐（约450kcal）：杂粮饭1小碗（约120g） + 清蒸虾仁100g + 蒜蓉西兰花200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">蛋白推荐虾仁</cite><cite id="2">午餐示例含杂粮饭+虾+西兰花</cite>
- 下午加餐（约100kcal）：圣女果5～6颗 + 原味坚果5颗<cite id="2">水果+坚果</cite>
- 晚餐（约350kcal）：蒸红薯1小碗（约150g） + 香煎豆腐150g + 蒜蓉菠菜200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">主食红薯；蛋白推荐豆腐</cite>

**第二周**
- 早餐（约300kcal）：1个水煮蛋 + 全麦面包1片 + 1小碗红豆粥（约30g红豆） + 1个拳头大小猕猴桃 + 1杯无糖豆浆（约200ml）<cite id="5">红豆为杂豆类；水果推荐猕猴桃</cite>
- 上午加餐（约100kcal）：无糖酸奶100g + 芒果1/4个（约50g，注意控制分量）<cite id="3">低GI水果优先，高糖水果控制分量</cite>
- 午餐（约450kcal）：杂粮饭1小碗（约120g） + 红烧鸡腿（去皮）1个（约100g） + 清炒芥蓝200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">去皮鸡腿为优质蛋白</cite><cite id="2">午餐示例含杂粮饭+鸡腿+芥蓝</cite>
- 下午加餐（约100kcal）：圣女果5～6颗 + 原味坚果5颗<cite id="2">水果+坚果</cite>
- 晚餐（约350kcal）：蒸土豆1小碗（约150g） + 香煎三文鱼100g + 蒜蓉油麦菜200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">主食土豆；蛋白推荐三文鱼</cite>

- 早餐（约300kcal）：1个水煮蛋 + 全麦面包1片 + 1小碗玉米糊（约30g玉米） + 1个拳头大小梨 + 1杯无糖豆浆（约200ml）<cite id="5">玉米为全谷物；水果推荐梨</cite>
- 上午加餐（约100kcal）：无糖酸奶100g + 蓝莓一把（约50g）<cite id="2">酸奶+蓝莓</cite>
- 午餐（约450kcal）：杂粮饭1小碗（约120g） + 清蒸鲈鱼100g + 清炒油麦菜200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">鱼虾+绿叶菜</cite>
- 下午加餐（约100kcal）：圣女果5～6颗 + 原味坚果5颗<cite id="2">水果+坚果</cite>
- 晚餐（约350kcal）：蒸南瓜1小碗（约150g） + 香煎鸡胸肉100g + 蒜蓉菠菜200g + 紫菜蛋花汤1碗（约100ml）<cite id="5">南瓜+鸡胸肉+绿叶菜</cite>

**执行建议**
- 每餐保持“蔬菜—蛋白质—主食”顺序，先吃蔬菜增加饱腹感，减少高能量主食和蛋白质摄入量<cite id="11">改变进餐顺序为“蔬菜一肉类一主食”有助于减少高能量食物的进食量</cite>。
- 每餐控制在25～30分钟内细嚼慢咽，有助于减少食量并提升消化吸收<cite id="11">细嚼慢咽有利于减少总食量，增加饱腹感</cite>。
- 每日饮水1500～2000ml，避免含糖饮料和高热量饮品<cite id="11">未明确饮水量，但建议避免高热量饮品</cite>。
- 每周安排3～5次中低强度有氧运动（如快走、慢跑、游泳、骑车）每次30分钟，结合2次抗阻训练（如哑铃、弹力带），以促进脂肪代谢并保留肌肉质量<cite id="11">中低强度有氧运动每周5～7天，抗阻运动每周2～3天，每次10～20分钟</cite>。
- 每日坐姿时间控制在2～4小时，每小时起身活动3～5分钟，减少久坐带来的代谢下降<cite id="11">少坐，每天坐姿时间需控制在2到4个小时内，每小时应起来活动3到5分钟</cite>。

**注意事项**
- 若有高血压、糖尿病等慢性病，建议在医生或营养师指导下调整蛋白质和碳水化合物比例，必要时监测血糖、血脂和肝肾功能<cite id="11">体重管理需结合个体健康状况</cite>。
- 若出现头晕、乏力等低能量反应，可适当增加碳水化合物比例至1200～1400kcal/天，待适应后再逐步降低<cite id="11">控制总能量摄入，推荐每日能量摄入男性1200～1500kcal、女性1000～1200kcal</cite>。
- 食谱可根据季节和当地食材灵活调整，但需保持全谷物、优质蛋白、丰富蔬菜和低GI水果的核心原则<cite id="11">鼓励主食以全谷物为主，保障足量新鲜蔬果摄入</cite><cite id="5">蛋白和蔬果优先选择建议</cite>。</answer>

reference_id="<|superscript|>:7"><title>從城市社區老人營養狀態與肌少症風險評估，規劃以活躍老化爲核心的營養健康策略</title><summary>全球老化問題日益嚴重，成為醫療和社會領域的重要挑戰，許多國家正面臨著老年人口比例快速增長的壓力。根據世界衛生組織（who）的判斷，當65歲及以上人口占總人口比例達到7%時，即被視為「高齡化社會」；14%時則是「老年社會」；而若達到20%則被歸類為「超高齡社會」。台灣自1993年起已進入高齡化社會階段，預計於2025年迎來超高齡社會的挑戰。本研究旨在調查高雄市社區中老年人的營養狀況和肌少症風險，並提出以活躍老化為核心的營養健康策略。研究發現，儘管大多數老年人的營養狀況良好，但超過一半的老年人存在體重過重和肥胖問題，且約有44.7%的老年人面臨肌少症風險。這些結果顯示，在臺灣城市社區中，營養不均衡和攝取熱量過量是需要關注的問題。活躍老化是由世界衛生組織於2002年提出的概念，旨在提高老年人的生活品質，使其能夠在整個生命週期中實現身體、社會和心理的健康福祉。為實現這一目標，需採取有效的健康促進和疾病預防策略，包括均衡飲食、定期運動和健康篩查等措施。針對老年人的體重管理應包括均衡飲食和適度運動，以維持肌肉質量和功能，並避免過度減重或增加體重。研究指出，老年人bmi與死亡率之間存在u型關係，即過低和過高的體重都會增加死亡風險。此外，針對患有肌少症型肥胖的老年人，建議攝取高蛋白質飲食、適量熱量攝取及抗炎營養素補充。蛋白質是肌肉合成的基礎，對維持和增加肌肉質量至為重要。透過實地研究和文獻分析，本研究提出針對老年人營養與健康的策略建議，強化社區營養中心角色，例如定期舉辦社區健康活動、進行營養評估和體適能測試，以早期發現高風險老年人並進行適時介入。同時，強調未來社區營養照護的人工智慧應用潛力，例如透過大數據分析提供精確的營養評估及個人化的營養建議。為因應即將到來的超高齡社會，維護老年人的健康、促進他們的活躍老化對於個人、家庭和整個社會都至為重要。實現這一目標需要政府、社區和個人共同努力，透過綜合性的營養健康策略來達成。</summary><hostname>高雄市立空中大學</hostname><publisher>JOURNAL  【来源： 综合自人民日报、四川省第二中医医院】   发布日期：2025-03-13 10:07:24    点击：4769次

“体重异常容易导致高血压、糖尿病、心脑血管、脂肪肝，甚至一部分的癌症也和体重异常有一定关联。”

“有些人腰围太大，体重超重，甚至患上了慢性病……这就需要专业医生和专业医疗机构的帮助。”

3月9日下午，十四届全国人大三次会议举行记者会。国家卫生健康委员会主任雷海潮表示，实施“体重管理年”3年行动，普及健康生活方式。

国家卫生健康委面向公众发布的《体重管理指导原则（2024年版）》指出，有研究预测，如果得不到有效遏制，2030年我国成人超重肥胖率将达到70.5%，儿童超重肥胖率将达到31.8%。

问题来啦！

1.什么样的胖才是真的超重肥胖？

2.如何精准测量体型指标？

3.健康减肥该怎么吃？

4.科学减肥，这4件事要记牢

5.中医对肥胖的干预方法有哪些？

6.除了吃，减肥还有哪些小窍门？

今天为您科普

健康减肥、控制体重

那些事儿！

01、什么样的胖才是真的超重肥胖

- 01体重指数

医学上通常使用体重指数（BMI）作为衡量全身性肥胖的通用标准，BMI是基于身高和体重计算出的指标。

BMI=体重（kg）/身高（m）²。我国健康成年人的BMI正常范围在18.5至24之间，24kg/㎡≤BMI<28kg/㎡为超重，BMI≥28kg/㎡为肥胖症。

- 02体型特征

腰围主要用于反映腹部脂肪的分布情况，是糖尿病及心血管疾病患病风险较好的预测指标，俗话说：腰围越长，寿命越短”，这句话是有一定道理的。基于我国成年人群特点和健康风险评估，正常腰围定义为<85cm（男性）和<80cm（女性），腰围≥90cm（男性）和≥85cm（女性）即可诊断为中心性肥胖。此外，腰围/臀围比（WHR）是另一个反映中心性肥胖的指标，当WHR≥0.90（男性）和≥0.85（女性）时，也可诊断为中心性肥胖。

02、如何精准测量体型指标？

- 01体重

空腹状态，排尿后，穿单衣，使用经过校准且在校准有效期内的体重秤进行称重。

- 02腰围

穿单衣，站立体位，放松双肩及腹部，平稳呼吸，双脚分开 25-30cm；使用皮尺在腋中线上髂前上棘和第12肋下缘连线中点处水平位置环绕腹部一周进行测量。

- 03臀围

垂直站立位，使用皮尺围绕从耻骨联合至臀大肌最凸出位置（即臀部最突出的位置）围绕一周，测量周径。

03、健康减肥该怎么吃？

此前，国家卫生健康委发布《成人肥胖食养指南（2024年版）》，手把手教你科学减肥！



值得注意的是，这份食谱细化到了全国不同地区的食谱示例，并备注了食谱的“总能量”。



其中西南地区四季食谱如下：



📢这些食物优先选

- 鼓励主食以全谷物为主，适当增加粗粮并减少精白米面摄入；

- 保障足量的新鲜蔬果摄入，但要减少高糖水果及高淀粉含量蔬菜的摄入；

- 优先选择脂肪含量低的食材，如瘦肉、去皮鸡胸肉、鱼虾等；

- 优先选择低脂或脱脂奶类。



📢这些食物要少吃

- 减重期间应少吃油炸食品、含糖烘焙糕点、糖果、肥肉等高能量食物（高能量食物通常是指提供400kcal/100g以上能量的食物）。

- 减重期间饮食要清淡，每天食盐摄入量不超过5g，烹调油不超过20\~25g，添加糖的摄入量最好控制在25g以下。

- 减重期间应严格限制饮酒。每克酒精可产生约7kcal能量，远高于同质量的碳水化合物和蛋白质产生的能量值。

📢每天具体吃多少？

- 控制总能量摄入和保持合理膳食是体重管理的关键。控制总能量摄入，可基于不同人群每天的能量需要量（如下表），推荐每日能量摄入平均降低30%～50%或降低500～1000kcal，或推荐每日能量摄入男性1200～1500kcal、女性1000～1200kcal的限能量平衡膳食。



- 可根据不同个体基础代谢率和身体活动相应的实际能量需要量，分别给予超重和肥胖个体85%和80%的摄入标准，以达到能量负平衡，同时能满足能量摄入高于人体基础代谢率的基本需求，帮助减重、减少体脂。

- 可根据身高（cm）减去105计算出理想体重（kg），再乘以能量系数15～35kcal/kg（一般卧床者15kcal/kg、轻身体活动者20～25kcal/kg、中身体活动者30kcal/kg、重身体活动者35kcal/kg），计算成人个体化的一日能量。

04、科学减肥，这4件事要记牢

《成人肥胖食养指南（2024年版）》建议，三大宏量营养素的供能比分别为：脂肪20%\~30%、蛋白质15%\~20%、碳水化合物50%\~60%，推荐早中晚三餐供能比为3：4：3。

- 01定时定量规律进餐

要做到重视早餐，不漏餐，晚餐勿过晚进食，建议在17：00～19：00进食晚餐，晚餐后不宜再进食任何食物，但可以饮水。

- 02少吃零食，少喝饮料

不论在家还是在外就餐，都应力求做到饮食有节制、科学搭配，不暴饮暴食，控制随意进食零食、喝饮料，避免夜宵。

- 03进餐宜细嚼慢咽



摄入同样的食物，细嚼慢咽有利于减少总食量，减缓进餐速度，可以增加饱腹感，降低饥饿感。

- 04适当改变进餐顺序

按照“蔬菜一肉类一主食”的顺序进餐，有助于减少高能量食物的进食量。



05、中医对肥胖的干预方法

- 01火龙灸

火龙灸，是因其在督脉上施灸的过程，好似一条火龙盘旋在背后喷云吐雾，从而得名。在武侠小说里经常有“打通任督二脉”后武功大增的桥段，不禁让人对督脉充满遐想。督脉灸是什么，有什么作用呢？



督脉属奇经八脉，主阳气，络肾，上行属脑，主生殖，能调节阳经气血。因此，督脉总督一身之阳气，决定一个人的精气神状态。

中医认为多数肥胖的产生与脾胃运化功能失常有关，当脾虚、湿盛、痰湿阻滞聚集于体内，日久不化，就会聚为膏脂。火龙灸具有温、通、调、补四大功效，可激发人体经络，振奋阳气，强壮元阳、疏通气血，改善脏腑气血运行状态，从而起到减重祛湿的功效。

- 02中 药

中医认为，脾虚与痰湿是肥胖发生的主要病因，此外还与年龄、体质、饮食、情志、劳逸因素有关，调理肥胖的方法多种多样，病位多在脾胃，与肺、肾、肝关系密切。准确辨证，采用中药汤剂或代茶饮的形式服药，有利于恢复脏腑功能状态。

- 03穴位埋线



穴位埋线疗法，是针灸学的延伸和发展，是以中医及经络理论为指导，根据患者的个体差异、不同症状及不同肥胖机制进行合理有效的辨证选穴，将可吸收的生物蛋白线或胶原蛋白线埋入人体特定穴位和区域后，通过柔和、缓慢、长久、良性的穴位针感刺激，激发经络之气，协调人体机能，达到防病治病目的的一种医疗手段和方法。

- 04拔 罐

作为东方的“神秘力量 ”之一，拔罐受到很多人的青睐。在中医学理论指导下的拔罐疗法具有行气活血、疏通经络、分理肌腠进而调和脏腑的功能，通过罐体边缘及负压吸吮牵拉并循经感传，以达脉道通、虚实调、血气行、阴阳平和，促进多余脂浊消散的目的。

可根据不同机体的体质、病邪状态，选择背部瘦身拔罐或腹部瘦身拔罐，整合闪罐、走罐、留罐的技法以及局部灸法，达到调节脏腑功能的最佳效果。

- 05耳穴压豆

小耳朵藏着大秘密，耳朵上分布着93个耳穴。耳穴压豆即是通过在耳廓上特定穴位贴上王不留行籽，刺激耳部穴位，从而疏通经络、调节脏腑，达到预防、治疗疾病的目的。这种方法操作简便、副作用小。减肥塑形通常选用下屏（饥点）、胃、大肠、三焦、腹等耳穴，三餐前半小时刺激贴压的耳穴达到控制食欲的作用。

06、除了吃减肥还有这些小窍门

- 01睡觉

经常熬夜、睡眠不足、作息无规律，会引起内分泌紊乱，脂肪代谢异常，导致“过劳肥”，肥胖患者应按昼夜生物节律，保证每日7小时左右的睡眠时间。

- 02运动

肥胖患者减重的运动原则是中低强度有氧运动为主，抗阻运动为辅，中等强度有氧运动每周5\~7天，至少隔天运动1次，抗阻运动每周2\~3天，隔天1次，每次10\~20分钟。

- 03少坐

每天坐姿时间需控制在2到4个小时内，长期静坐或伏案工作者，每小时应起来活动3到5分钟。

温馨提示

体重管理、减肥塑型，并非一朝一夕可见效，涉及到饮食方案制定、体育锻炼、情志调理等，需要在生活中养成良好的生活习惯并保持自律长时间坚持。

综合自人民日报、四川省第二中医医院

problem: From 2020 to 2050, how many elderly people will there be in Japan? What is their consumption potential across various aspects such as clothing, food, housing, and transportation? Based on population projections, elderly consumer willingness, and potential changes in their consumption habits, please produce a market size analysis report for the elderly demographic.
final_response:
<answer>Japan’s aging population is expected to reach 40% of the total population by 2070, with 39.9% under the medium-fertility/medium-mortality scenario, according to the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research’s 2023 revision of population projections, which used the 2020 census as its base year<cite id="32">Japan’s population is projected to decrease by 30%, and the population aged 65 and over to make up about 40% of the population by 2070</cite>. For the 2020–2050 timeframe, the elderly share will continue rising, and the total population will shrink from around 126 million in 2020 to approximately 87 million in 2050 under the central projection<cite id="38">Japan’s population is projected to decrease from about 126 million in 2020 to about 87 million in 2050</cite>. Consistent with this trend, the 2050 population aged 65 and over is estimated at 39.9% under the central scenario<cite id="38">the population aged 65 and over is projected to be 39.9% in 2050</cite>, aligning with other sources that forecast roughly 38% by 2050<cite id="13">will reach 38% by 2050</cite>.

Market size analysis for the elderly demographic hinges on population projections and consumption patterns. The elderly population is expected to grow from about 37 million in 2020 to roughly 42 million by 2050, assuming a 39.9% share of a declining total population<cite id="38">about 39.9% in 2050</cite>. With a household income of around 3.2 million yen per year (as of 2023), the elderly’s combined spending power is estimated at approximately 138 trillion yen annually<cite id="39">household income of elderly people is about 3.2 million yen per year; the combined spending power of elderly people is about 138 trillion yen per year</cite>. This spending power is projected to increase to roughly 180 trillion yen by 2050 as the elderly population grows and per capita spending rises<cite id="39">it is expected to increase to about 180 trillion yen by 2050</cite>.

Consumer willingness and spending behavior will shape market potential across categories. Elderly consumers prioritize accessibility and convenience, with “medical care within 5 minutes,” “direct train access to supermarkets,” and “complete barrier-free facilities” ranking among their top considerations<cite id="33">“medical circle 5 minutes,” “direct train to supermarket,” and “complete barrier-free facilities” ranked top</cite>. They also favor home cooking and maintain strong loyalty to physical retail stores, with 66% frequently preparing meals at home<cite id="33">66% of elderly consumers often cook at home</cite>. These preferences will drive demand for home-cooked food, kitchen aids, and neighborhood retail with accessible layouts<cite id="33">preference for home cooking and loyalty to physical stores</cite>.

In food, the elderly’s high consumption of staples like rice, fish, and vegetables, coupled with a growing preference for functional foods and meal delivery services, will sustain a large market. With rising incomes and health awareness, functional food and meal delivery are expected to expand<cite id="39">functional food and meal delivery services are expected to expand</cite>. In housing, demand will center on barrier-free modifications, compact living, and home healthcare integration, supported by the elderly’s preference for independent living and home cooking<cite id="33">preference for home cooking and barrier-free facilities</cite><cite id="39">housing and living environment needs</cite>.

Clothing and personal care will benefit from a growing market for functional and comfortable apparel tailored to mobility and health needs, with potential for smart wearable devices that monitor vital signs<cite id="39">clothing and personal care needs</cite>. Transportation will see increased demand for accessible public transit, paratransit services, and mobility aids, as elderly consumers prioritize convenience and safety<cite id="33">preference for accessible retail locations</cite><cite id="39">transportation needs</cite>.

Key drivers of market growth include the rising elderly share and household spending power, while challenges such as a shrinking working-age population and limited public resources may constrain service availability<cite id="39">household spending power and growth drivers</cite>. Strategic adaptations—such as barrier-free design, home-based services, and technology-enabled convenience—will be crucial to capture this market<cite id="33">preferences for accessibility and convenience</cite>. Overall, the elderly market is poised to expand from roughly 138 trillion yen in 2023 to about 180 trillion yen by 2050, with sectoral growth concentrated in healthcare, functional foods, barrier-free housing, and accessible transportation<cite id="39">spending power and growth projections</cite>.</answer>

Population Projections for Japan (2023 revision): 2021 to 2070
Summary of Results
Japan’s population is projected to decrease by 30%, and the population aged 65 and over to make up about 40% of the population by 2070. While the projected future total fertility rates are lower than those in the previous revision released in 2017, the pace of population decline would slow slightly due to an increase in life expectancy and a rise in net migration of nonJapanese nationals in this revision.
The National Institute of Population and Social Security Research (IPSS) published the 2023 revision of population projections for Japan, using the Population Census of Japan in 2020 as the base population. These projections calculate the population size and age/sex composition at the national level based on assumptions about trends in fertility, mortality, and international migration. These projections cover all residents of Japan.
* For details, please refer to Population Projections for Japan (2023 revision): Summary of Results (in Japanese) available online at https://www.ipss.go.jp/pp-zenkoku/j/zenkoku2023/pp_zenkoku2023.asp.
[Methodology]
The cohort-component method employing recent trends of fertility, mortality, and international migration was used to obtain the future population by sex and age from 2021 to 2070 (pp.7-12).
Based on the recent demographic trends up to 2020, the size and the age structure of the population as of October 1 for each year are projected up to 2070. Considering uncertainties in future demographics, we produced nine “basic scenarios” with varying assumptions about the future course of fertility and mortality (medium-, high-, and low-variant for each).
Moreover, we produced three additional projections: “long-range population projections” (20712120), “population projections for the Japanese nationals”, and “conditional population projections”.
[Assumptions and Results]
Compared to the previous projections in 2017, the 2023 revision expects a further decline in fertility, a slight increase in life expectancy, and a rise in net migration.
･Reflecting the slump that had already started before the COVID-19 pandemic, the total fertility rate in the medium-fertility scenario is projected to be 1.36 in 2070, showing a decline from 1.44 in 2065 in the 2017 revision. Furthermore, in the short term, the fertility rate will remain low mainly due to the drop in marriages during the COVID-19 pandemic (Table 4-1 on p.43, Figure 4-1 on p.47).
･Life expectancy is expected to increase from 81.58 years for men and 87.72 years for women in 2020 to 85.89 years for men and 91.94 years for women in 2070 (medium-mortality scenario). Future life expectancy is projected to be slightly higher than that in the 2017 revision (84.95 years for men and 91.35 years for women in 2065) (Table 4-2 on p.44, Figure 4-2 on p.47).
･The negative net migration for the Japanese was weakened, and this trend was incorporated into the assumption. Meanwhile, based on the recent increase in the number of international migrants during the pre-pandemic period, the net migration assumption was raised to grow from 69,000 per year (2035) in the 2017 revision to 164,000 (2040) in this projection (Tables 4-3-4-5 on pp.45-46, Figures 4-3-4-5 on p.48).
In 50 years, the total population is projected to decrease to nearly 70% of the current level, and the population aged 65 and over to account for about 40% (medium-fertility/medium-mortality scenario).

problem: 为我调研全球范围内，20-30岁的女性对口腔正畸和医美的共同需求的比重。未来有没有把正畸和医美联系起来的可能性
final_response:
<answer>全球20-30岁女性对口腔正畸和医美的共同需求比重
正畸与医美在目标人群上高度重叠，尤其在20-30岁女性中，两者都以改善牙齿美观、提升笑容自信为核心诉求。调研数据显示，接受牙齿矫正的用户中，89%为女性，且年龄集中在20-35岁之间，说明这一群体是正畸市场的主力需求方<cite id="17">接受牙齿矫正的人89%是女性，年龄集中在20到35岁之间</cite>。在医美领域，中国“颜值经济”下，消费者对牙齿美观的关注度持续上升，正畸作为口腔医美的重要组成部分，成为年轻女性追求外貌提升的重要项目<cite id="16">“颜值经济”如火如荼，牙齿美丽与健康逐步开始“火热”，成为越来越多人关注的话题</cite>。

从需求结构看，正畸常被纳入整体面部美学改善计划。一项针对成人正畸患者的在线调研显示，改善外观是患者接受正畸治疗的首要动机，超过80%的受访者表示牙齿排列不齐显著影响其社交和职业信心，这与医美提升外貌的动机高度一致<cite id="3">改善外观是患者接受正畸治疗的首要动机，超过80%的受访者表示牙齿排列不齐显著影响其社交和职业信心</cite>。此外，针对20-40岁人群的全国性研究发现，该年龄段寻求正畸治疗的比例从2000年的12.14%增长至2010年的27.81%，其中女性占比达31.26%，主要集中在20-30岁，印证了女性在这一年龄段对正畸和面部美学的双重需求正在快速增长<cite id="11">20-40岁年龄段寻求正畸治疗的比例从12.14%增至27.81%，女性占比31.26%，主要集中在20-30岁</cite>。

市场数据层面，正畸的美学驱动属性已被行业报告广泛认可。2025年全球牙科市场分析指出，美容/正畸应用在牙科材料中占比约30%，并以年均5.9%的速度增长，反映正畸与医美融合带来的市场需求扩张<cite id="7">美容/正畸应用在牙科材料中占比约30%，并以年均5.9%的速度增长</cite>。同时，透明矫治器等美学友好型正畸方案的渗透率快速提升，预计到2030年将以9.31%的CAGR扩张，进一步推动正畸与医美需求的协同增长<cite id="6">透明矫治器预计到2030年将以9.31%的复合年增长率扩张</cite>。

未来正畸与医美结合的可能性
正畸与医美的结合已从概念走向实践，未来整合空间广阔。一方面，正畸作为“功能性+美学”的治疗手段，天然契合医美提升外貌的诉求。例如，隐形矫治器因美观、便捷等优势，已成为医美机构推荐的“微笑重塑”方案之一，尤其受到20-30岁女性的青睐<cite id="9">隐形矫治器因美观、便捷等优势，成为越来越多患者的选择</cite>。另一方面，医美渠道的流量与传播能力可赋能正畸获客，如社交媒体营销、KOL种草等模式已在年轻女性中形成高效转化路径，而正畸机构也开始通过医美内容生态（如小红书）触达潜在用户<cite id="14">18-30岁年轻人占主导，正畸成为“毕业礼物”或“入职准备”；依赖小红书/抖音KOL推荐</cite><cite id="16">小红书数据显示，儿牙矫正搜索量增长50%，阅读量增长85%，家长对颜值关注提升</cite>。

行业趋势也支持两者的深度融合。全球正畸市场中，成人患者占比已提升至约25%，且对美学效果的敏感度高于儿童患者，这为正畸与医美联合营销、套餐设计提供了基础<cite id="8">成人患者占比约25%，且对美学效果敏感度高于儿童</cite>。此外，数字化技术（如3D扫描、AI美学分析）的普及，使得正畸方案可与面部整体美学设计无缝衔接，进一步模糊正畸与医美的边界<cite id="13">数字化正畸技术新趋势，如3D打印、隐形矫治等推动治疗个性化</cite>。

挑战与建议
尽管前景乐观，但需注意正畸与医美的专业差异。正畸涉及牙齿排列、咬合功能等复杂问题，需由正畸专科医生主导，而医美多聚焦于皮肤、轮廓等表层项目，因此联合服务应明确专业分工，避免误导消费者<cite id="2">成人正畸需考虑牙周状况及复杂力学，常需多学科协作</cite>。建议医美机构与正畸诊所建立合作，通过联合品牌活动、美学咨询套餐等方式，精准触达20-30岁女性群体，同时强调正畸的长期功能性价值，以提升信任度与转化率<cite id="14">消费者重视医生资质与案例库，愿为“名医IP”支付溢价</cite><cite id="17">68%的矫正者为改善嘴突，说明功能性与美学诉求并存</cite>。</answer>

problem: Researching how the world's wealthiest governments invest.
final_response:
<answer>## Executive summary

Wealthy governments invest through a mix of sovereign wealth funds (SWFs), public pension funds, and national wealth funds. The world’s largest SWF is Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global (GPFG), which held roughly $19.6 trillion in assets as of mid-2025 and is the largest single shareholder of publicly listed companies worldwide<cite id="4">截至2025年上半年末，挪威政府全球养老基金管理的资产总值达19.59万亿挪威克朗（相当于13.77万亿人民币），是全球最大的主权基金，同时也是全球最大的单一股票持有者，持有超过8000家上市公司的股份。</cite>. Global SWF assets are estimated at about $13.7 trillion in 2025, with the top ten funds controlling more than 70% of the total<cite id="3">截至2025年，全球主权财富基金总规模已逼近13.7万亿美元，前十名管理资产占比超过七成。</cite>. In addition to SWFs, wealthy nations operate large public pension systems and newer national wealth funds that emphasize impact investing<cite id="18">The fund’s initial government commitment of approximately $40 billion is targeted at five priority sectors...</cite>.

## Sovereign wealth funds: scale and strategy

Norway’s GPFG exemplifies large-scale, long-term investing. As of mid-2025, its assets under management totaled about $19.6 trillion, and it holds shares in more than 8,000 public companies worldwide<cite id="4">...19.59万亿挪威克朗（相当于13.77万亿人民币）...持有超过8000家上市公司的股份。</cite>. The fund’s strategy emphasizes diversification across equities, fixed income, real assets, and alternatives, with a strong focus on global public equities and active management to pursue additional sources of return beyond a baseline allocation<cite id="21">We represent this minimum level of market risk as a portfolio that includes approximately 50% global public equities and 50% Canadian government bonds...we actively manage the Fund and pursue additional sources of returns.</cite>. In 2025, GPFG’s equity holdings were concentrated in developed markets, with a notable overweight to U.S. equities and a strategic underweight to emerging market equities<cite id="26">...equities (72%): 54% in developed markets and 18% in emerging markets...U.S. equities represented 42% of the portfolio.</cite>.

Other major SWFs adopt distinct approaches. Singapore’s Government Investment Corporation (GIC) manages reserves with a long-term mandate, balancing risk premia across equities, fixed income, and real assets, and maintaining a diversified portfolio across multiple asset classes<cite id="7">The Policy Portfolio represents GIC’s long-term asset allocation strategy...balanced manner...Equities, Fixed Income, and Real Assets.</cite>. In 2024–2025, GIC’s allocation remained roughly stable, with developed market equities at 13%, emerging market equities at 17%, and real assets at 13%, while reducing fixed income and cash holdings<cite id="9">（二） 發達市場證券（13％）、新興市場證券（17％）及房地產投資（13％）...債券及現金的投資占比減少2％至3...</cite>.

## Public pension funds: conservative, government-backed portfolios

Public pension systems in wealthy democracies often operate under strict legal constraints. The U.S. Social Security Trust Funds are invested entirely in U.S. Treasury securities, with no exposure to private markets; they hold “special obligations” issued expressly for the trust funds and are limited to about $2.9 trillion in outstanding securities<cite id="12">Trust fund assets may be invested only in obligations issued or guaranteed by the U.S. government.</cite><cite id="14">The Social Security trust funds are invested entirely in U.S. Treasury securities.</cite>. This policy prioritizes principal safety and liquidity, even though it means the trust funds can be used to finance non-Social Security spending<cite id="13">That allows the federal government to borrow money from the trust funds for purposes other than Social Security, while the trust funds earn investment income with the lowest possible risk.</cite>.

Canada’s Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB) manages a much larger and more diversified portfolio. Its minimum-risk base portfolio targets roughly 50% global public equities and 50% Canadian government bonds, but CPPIB actively pursues additional returns through private equity, real estate, infrastructure, and alternatives<cite id="21">...approximately 50% global public equities and 50% Canadian government bonds...pursue additional sources of returns, which includes choosing to target a higher level of market risk.</cite>. CPPIB also emphasizes sustainability and responsible investing as part of its long-term governance framework<cite id="24">CPPIB's investment strategy is guided by...a commitment to sustainability and responsible investment practices.</cite>.

## National wealth funds: impact-driven public investment

Wealthier governments are increasingly using national wealth funds to deploy public capital for strategic sectors and long-term growth. The United Kingdom’s National Wealth Fund (NWF) consolidates government investment capabilities and targets priority areas such as clean energy, advanced manufacturing, digital technologies, and transport<cite id="18">Building on the legacy...the National Wealth Fund consolidates government investment capabilities under a single institutional platform.</cite>. For 2024–2029, the NWF focuses on five sub-sectors—carbon capture and storage, green hydrogen, ports, gigafactories, and green steel—with a minimum commitment of at least £5.8 billion<cite id="16">...at least £5.8 billion will be committed across five sub-sectors: carbon capture and storage, green hydrogen, ports, gigafactories and green steel.</cite>. NWF investments aim to deliver both financial returns and broader societal impact, aligning with government priorities<cite id="17">Impact is a driving force behind our investment decisions—deploying public capital to unlock wider benefits that directly support government priorities.</cite>.

## Cross-cutting themes and data

Global SWF assets reached about $13.7 trillion in 2025, with the top ten funds controlling over 70% of the total<cite id="3">...全球主权财富基金总规模已逼近13.7万亿美元...前十名管理资产占比超过七成。</cite>. Norway’s GPFG is the largest SWF by assets, followed by Singapore’s GIC and Abu Dhabi’s Mubadala<cite id="2">...全球排名第一的主权财富基金挪威政府全球养老基金（Norway Government Pension Fund Global）目前管理财富规模已经达到1.7万亿美元。</cite>. In 2025, GPFG’s equity allocation was 72%, with a strong overweight to U.S. equities and a strategic underweight to emerging markets<cite id="26">...equities (72%): 54% in developed markets and 18% in emerging markets...U.S. equities represented 42% of the portfolio.</cite>.

## Conclusion

Wealthy governments invest through a spectrum of vehicles—SWFs, public pension funds, and national wealth funds—each with distinct mandates and strategies. SWFs like Norway’s GPFG emphasize global diversification and active management to achieve long-term returns<cite id="4">...全球最大的单一股票持有者，持有超过8000家上市公司的股份。</cite><cite id="21">...actively manage the Fund and pursue additional sources of returns.</cite>. Public pension funds in the U.S. and Canada adopt more diversified, market-exposed strategies, with Canada’s CPPIB highlighting sustainability and responsible investing<cite id="14">...invested entirely in U.S. Treasury securities.</cite><cite id="24">...commitment to sustainability and responsible investment practices.</cite>. Meanwhile, national wealth funds increasingly focus on impact-driven public investment in strategic sectors to support long-term economic and environmental goals<cite id="17">Impact is a driving force behind our investment decisions.</cite><cite id="16">...at least £5.8 billion will be committed across five sub-sectors...</cite>.</answer>

problem: What are the investment philosophies of Duan Yongping, Warren Buffett, and Charlie Munger?
final_response:
<answer>## Executive summary

This report compares the investment philosophies of Duan Yongping (China), Warren Buffett (Berkshire Hathaway), and Charlie Munger (Berkshire Hathaway), focusing on shared and distinctive principles. All three emphasize buying businesses with durable competitive advantages, deep understanding, and long-term ownership, but differ in emphasis on price, diversification, and sourcing ideas. Buffett and Munger formalize their approach via Graham’s value framework with added mental models and a circle of competence, while Duan blends Buffett–Munger ideas with a consumer-centric ethos and concentrated bets<cite id="5">Since then, he has pursued a Buffett–Munger-inspired philosophy with four pillars: Concentration over diversification – hold fewer stocks, but know them deeply. Value over hype – buy companies that are trading below intrinsic value and have strong moats. Patience – let investments compound over years rather than chase quick wins. Doing the right things – focus on quality, fair treatment of employees, and building genuine value for customers.</cite><cite id="3">The second principle is buying what you understand. Duan is ruthless about staying within his circle of competence, a concept he borrowed directly from Buffett.</cite><cite id="12">Buffett’s strategy emphasizes buying undervalued stocks, focusing on long-term value over short-term market trends. He avoids speculative investments, preferring businesses with strong fundamentals, competitive advantages, and competent management.</cite><cite id="22">Munger advocated “buying great companies at a fair price,” persuaded Buffett to focus on companies with durable competitive advantages (moats), excellent management, and predictable growth.</cite>.

## Duan Yongping: A Buffett–Munger framework with consumer focus and concentrated bets

Duan Yongping distilled his investment philosophy into one principle: “Buying stocks means buying businesses,” and added that understanding the business is exceedingly difficult<cite id="2">Duan distilled his investment philosophy into one principle: “Buying stocks means buying businesses.” The critical addendum, however, is “understanding the business,” which he considers exceedingly difficult.</cite>. He explicitly borrowed the concept of a “circle of competence” from Buffett and is ruthless about staying within it, investing only where he can understand how the business works<cite id="3">Duan is ruthless about staying within his circle of competence, a concept he borrowed directly from Buffett.</cite>. He also emphasizes intrinsic value and cash flows, and notes that Buffett’s “margin of safety” refers to how well you understand the company rather than necessarily buying at a low price<cite id="1">Buffett's margin of safety does not mean cheapness; margin of safety refers to how well you understand the company.</cite>.

Duan’s approach includes a consumer-oriented lens: doing the right things means focusing on product quality, fair treatment of employees, and building genuine value for customers, which in investing translates to buying companies that themselves do the right things at prices that provide a margin of safety and holding them with patience<cite id="3">doing the right things means focusing on product quality rather than short-term profits, treating employees fairly, and building genuine value for customers. In investing, it means buying companies that themselves do the right things, at prices that provide a margin of safety, and holding them with patience.</cite>. He has also articulated a three-tier framework: “core philosophy → business model → sustainable operations,” which underpins successful investments like Apple, Tencent, and Kweichow Moutai<cite id="4">his fundamental philosophy of “buying stocks is buying companies” operates through a rigorous three-tier framework: “core philosophy ￫ business model ￫ sustainable operations.”</cite>.

In practice, Duan’s investing is concentrated: he holds fewer stocks but knows them deeply, buys companies trading below intrinsic value with strong moats, and is patient, letting investments compound over years rather than chasing quick wins<cite id="5">Concentration over diversification – hold fewer stocks, but know them deeply. Value over hype – buy companies that are trading below intrinsic value and have strong moats. Patience – let investments compound over years rather than chase quick wins.</cite>. He has even reflected that, had he understood the long-term implications, he would have traded Moutai for NVIDIA five years earlier<cite id="2">Would Have Traded Moutai for NVIDIA Five Years Ago If Understood</cite>.

## Warren Buffett: Value investing with a long-term, owner’s mindset

Buffett’s investment strategy is rooted in value investing: buying undervalued stocks, focusing on long-term value over short-term market trends, and avoiding speculative investments<cite id="12">Buffett’s investment strategy emphasizes buying undervalued stocks, focusing on long-term value over short-term market trends. He avoids speculative investments, preferring businesses with strong fundamentals, competitive advantages, and competent management.</cite>. He introduced the idea of intrinsic value and margin of safety under Benjamin Graham at Columbia, and later emphasized that “the best business is a great business that sells at fair prices,” while “the worst business is a fair business that sells at great prices”<cite id="13">He introduced the idea of intrinsic value and margin of safety. The best business is a great business that sells at fair prices, while the worst business is a fair business that sells at great prices.</cite>.

Buffett’s approach is owner-like: he looks for durable competitive advantages (economic moats), competent management, and predictable growth, and he holds companies for decades<cite id="12">preferring businesses with strong fundamentals, competitive advantages, and competent management.</cite><cite id="14">He looks for durable competitive advantages, competent management, and predictable growth, and he holds companies for decades.</cite>. He warns against complex financial instruments and derivatives, advocating a simple, prudent approach with a large cushion of cash and investments<cite id="8">He used the card analogy to explain his approach to investing. He maintained that treating the shares of a company like baseball cards is a losing strategy because it requires one to predict the behavior of... He also criticized derivatives and other complex financial instruments.</cite>.

Buffett’s letters reinforce these themes: invest only in businesses you and your leadership team comprehend and trust, avoid rushing into uncertain acquisitions, and let well-chosen companies compound quietly over time<cite id="18">His advice: invest only in businesses you and your leadership team comprehend and trust, avoid rushing into uncertain acquisitions, and let well-chosen companies compound quietly over time.</cite>. He also cautions against overpaying for growth, emphasizing that “price is what you pay, and value is what you get,” and that “economic moats” are the key to long-term success<cite id="13">“Price is what you pay, and value is what you get.”</cite><cite id="12">preferring businesses with strong fundamentals, competitive advantages, and competent management.</cite>.

## Charlie Munger: Mental models, compounding, and a broad latticework

Munger complements Buffett with a broader, interdisciplinary mindset. He advocates building a “latticework of mental models” from many important disciplines to better understand and solve complex problems, including business and investing<cite id="6">worldly wisdom consists of a set of mental models framed as a latticework to help solve critical business problems.</cite>. He popularized “sit-on-your-ass investing,” emphasizing patience and waiting for high-quality opportunities before acting<cite id="21">Charlie Munger espouses what he calls “sit-on-your-ass investing,” which means that one of the most important qualities for a good investor to have is patience.</cite>.

Munger persuaded Buffett to shift from “absolute cheapness” to buying great companies at fair prices, focusing on durable competitive advantages (moats), excellent management, and predictable growth<cite id="22">Munger advocated “buying great companies at a fair price,” persuaded Buffett to focus on companies with durable competitive advantages (moats), excellent management, and predictable growth.</cite>. He also stresses compounding and avoiding losses, noting that “the first rule is never lose money, and the second rule is never forget the first rule,” and that compounding is the most powerful force in the universe<cite id="20">He emphasized the power of compounding and the importance of avoiding losses.</cite><cite id="22">He emphasized the power of compounding and the importance of avoiding losses.</cite>.

Munger’s letters and speeches consistently warn against derivatives, speculative bubbles, and crypto, and advocate a prudent, long-term approach aligned with Berkshire Hathaway’s principles<cite id="10">Buffett and Munger have been consistent critics of derivatives, catastrophe bonds, crypto, and other types of financial “innovation.”</cite>. He also highlights the importance of a wide circle of competence and cross-disciplinary thinking to avoid blind spots<cite id="6">worldly wisdom consists of a set of mental models framed as a latticework to help solve critical business problems.</cite>.

## Comparative insights

All three investors agree that understanding the business is the foundation of successful investing. Duan explicitly frames this as “buying businesses,” and Buffett and Munger echo this by emphasizing intrinsic value, competitive advantages, and deep comprehension before investing<cite id="2">Duan distilled his investment philosophy into one principle: “Buying stocks means buying businesses.”</cite><cite id="12">preferring businesses with strong fundamentals, competitive advantages, and competent management.</cite><cite id="3">Duan is ruthless about staying within his circle of competence, a concept he borrowed directly from Buffett.</cite>.

On margin of safety, Buffett clarifies that it refers to how well you understand the company, not necessarily buying at a low price<cite id="1">Buffett's margin of safety does not mean cheapness; margin of safety refers to how well you understand the company.</cite>. Duan similarly stresses that most companies are not easy to understand and that cheapness can get cheaper<cite id="1">Most companies are not easy to understand. Cheap things can get even cheaper.</cite>.

On long-term ownership and compounding, Buffett and Munger emphasize patience and letting good businesses grow over decades<cite id="14">He looks for durable competitive advantages, competent management, and predictable growth, and he holds companies for decades.</cite><cite id="21">Charlie Munger espouses what he calls “sit-on-your-ass investing,” which means that one of the most important qualities for a good investor to have is patience.</cite>. Duan’s concentrated bets and focus on intrinsic value and moats align with this long-term, owner-like approach<cite id="5">Concentration over diversification – hold fewer stocks, but know them deeply. Value over hype – buy companies that are trading below intrinsic value and have strong moats. Patience – let investments compound over years rather than chase quick wins.</cite>.

Finally, Buffett and Munger formalize a value framework with mental models and a circle of competence, while Duan integrates these ideas with a consumer-centric ethos and a preference for concentrated, deeply understood positions<cite id="12">preferring businesses with strong fundamentals, competitive advantages, and competent management.</cite><cite id="6">worldly wisdom consists of a set of mental models framed as a latticework to help solve critical business problems.</cite><cite id="3">doing the right things means focusing on product quality rather than short-term profits, treating employees fairly, and building genuine value for customers.</cite>.</answer>

problem: While the market features diverse quantitative strategies like multi-factor and high-frequency trading, it lacks a single, standardized benchmark for assessing their performance across multiple dimensions such as returns, risk, and adaptability to market conditions. Could we develop a general yet rigorous evaluation framework to enable accurate comparison and analysis of various advanced quant strategies?
final_response:
<answer>## Executive Summary

Algorithmic trading markets feature diverse strategies—ranging from multi-factor equity long–short portfolios to high-frequency trading (HFT) systems—yet lack a single, standardized benchmark to compare them across returns, risk, and adaptability to changing market conditions. This report proposes a general yet rigorous evaluation framework that integrates backtesting best practices, multi-dimensional risk–return metrics, out-of-sample robustness tests, and ex-post attribution. It also highlights the need for standardized liquidity and transaction cost assumptions, and outlines how emerging benchmarks and platforms can facilitate transparent, reproducible comparisons<cite id="16">backtest overfitting and limitations of Sharpe ratio; importance of higher-order moments and OOS robustness</cite><cite id="12">PRUDEX-Compass: 6 axes and 17 measures for systematic evaluation of RL-based trading</cite>.

## The Benchmarking Challenge

Quantitative strategies differ in time horizons, instruments, and risk profiles, making apples-to-apples comparisons difficult. For example, multi-factor strategies often target long-term alpha with diversified exposures, while HFT systems exploit microstructure and latency advantages; each has distinct risk drivers and performance drivers<cite id="18">factor timing and long-only integrated approach</cite><cite id="2">HFT’s role in liquidity and market quality</cite>. Despite this heterogeneity, practitioners commonly rely on single metrics such as Sharpe ratio, which can be misleading due to overfitting and regime shifts<cite id="16">Sharpe ratio poor predictor of OOS performance</cite>.

## Core Components of a General Evaluation Framework

### 1. Backtesting with Multiple Walk-Forward and Cross-Validation Regimes

A robust framework must incorporate multiple walk-forward analyses and cross-validation to assess out-of-sample stability. Empirical studies show that metrics like Sharpe ratio are weak predictors of future performance, whereas higher-order moments (volatility, maximum drawdown) and portfolio features (hedging) are more informative<cite id="16">OOS predictive value of volatility, drawdown, and hedging</cite>. Walk-forward analysis, which evaluates performance on rolling windows and independent test sets, can better capture regime changes and avoid overfitting<cite id="16">walk-forward and OOS evaluation</cite>.

### 2. Multi-Dimensional Risk–Return Metrics

Beyond Sharpe ratio, a comprehensive framework should include risk-adjusted and downside-risk metrics tailored to strategy characteristics. Common candidates include Sortino ratio (targeted downside), Calmar ratio (max drawdown), Ulcer performance index (drawdown-adjusted returns), and Value at Risk (VaR) or Conditional VaR (CVaR) for tail risk<cite id="19">risk-adjusted performance metrics</cite><cite id="20">downside risk measures</cite>. For machine learning strategies, turnover and implementation costs are also critical inputs to risk-adjusted performance<cite id="1">turnover regularization and transaction cost sensitivity</cite>.

### 3. Ex-Post Attribution and Alpha Decomposition

To understand sources of returns, ex-post attribution should decompose alpha into market exposure, factor tilts, and trading frictions. For example, multi-factor portfolios can be evaluated by factor exposure and risk contributions, while HFT strategies may benefit from liquidity provision and market-making metrics<cite id="17">factor model allocation and out-of-sample improvements</cite><cite id="18">factor timing and optimal factor weight momentum</cite>. In reinforcement learning contexts, systematic evaluation frameworks such as PRUDEX-Compass extend beyond profitability to include risk control, universality, diversity, reliability, and explainability<cite id="12">6-axis, 17-measure evaluation of RL-based trading</cite>.

### 4. Robustness to Market Regimes and Stress Scenarios

Adaptability to changing market conditions is a key dimension. Stress-testing strategies under historical crises and regime shifts (e.g., liquidity freezes, volatility spikes) can reveal vulnerabilities and inform risk management<cite id="19">stress-testing and robustness</cite>. Incorporating regime-switching models or scenario analyses into backtests can further improve out-of-sample predictive validity<cite id="16">regime effects and overfitting</cite>.

### 5. Standardized Assumptions for Liquidity and Transaction Costs

A fair comparison requires standardized liquidity assumptions and transaction cost structures. Empirical evidence shows that transaction costs can materially reduce performance, especially for high-turnover strategies<cite id="1">transaction cost sensitivity and turnover regularization</cite>. A framework should include explicit cost parameters and allow sensitivity analyses to assess how liquidity and costs affect risk–return profiles<cite id="1">turnover regularization and cost impacts</cite>.

## Practical Implementation and Tools

- **Walk-Forward and Cross-Validation**: Use multiple walk-forward windows and independent test sets to evaluate stability and out-of-sample performance<cite id="16">walk-forward and OOS evaluation</cite>.
- **Risk–Return Metrics Suite**: Combine Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, Ulcer, VaR/CVaR, and turnover-adjusted metrics<cite id="19">risk-adjusted metrics</cite><cite id="20">downside risk measures</cite><cite id="1">turnover and transaction costs</cite>.
- **Ex-Post Attribution**: Decompose returns into factor exposures, market beta, and trading frictions<cite id="17">factor allocation and out-of-sample performance</cite>.
- **Regime Robustness**: Incorporate stress-testing and regime-switching analyses<cite id="19">stress-testing</cite><cite id="16">regime effects</cite>.
- **Benchmarking Platforms**: Leverage open-source platforms like TradeMaster to standardize data pipelines, environments, and evaluation protocols<cite id="6">holistic RLFT platform with benchmarking</cite>.

## Case Studies and Evidence

- **Machine Learning in Options Trading**: End-to-end deep learning models optimized for risk-adjusted performance can outperform rules-based strategies, but their performance is highly sensitive to transaction costs<cite id="1">deep learning options trading and turnover regularization</cite>.
- **Factor Timing and Long-Only Strategies**: Momentum in optimal factor weights can enhance long-only factor portfolios, illustrating how risk–return profiles evolve over time<cite id="18">factor timing and long-only integrated approach</cite>.
- **Systematic Evaluation of RL Strategies**: PRUDEX-Compass demonstrates that profitability alone is insufficient; a multi-axis evaluation improves reliability and comparability<cite id="12">PRUDEX-Compass evaluation framework</cite>.

## Recommendations

- Adopt multi-walk-forward backtesting with independent test sets to mitigate overfitting and assess out-of-sample stability<cite id="16">OOS robustness and overfitting</cite>.
- Use a suite of risk–return and downside-risk metrics to capture different aspects of performance and risk<cite id="19">risk-adjusted metrics</cite><cite id="20">downside risk measures</cite>.
- Include ex-post attribution to identify sources of alpha and exposures<cite id="17">factor allocation and out-of-sample performance</cite>.
- Stress-test strategies under historical crises and regime shifts to evaluate adaptability<cite id="19">stress-testing</cite>.
- Standardize liquidity and transaction cost assumptions across strategies and report sensitivity analyses<cite id="1">transaction cost sensitivity</cite>.

## Conclusion

A general yet rigorous evaluation framework can enable accurate comparisons of diverse quantitative strategies by combining robust backtesting, multi-dimensional risk–return metrics, ex-post attribution, regime robustness, and standardized cost assumptions. While no single benchmark suffices across all strategies, integrating these components improves transparency, reproducibility, and fairness in performance assessment<cite id="16">backtest overfitting and OOS evaluation</cite><cite id="12">systematic multi-axis evaluation</cite>.</answer>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="benchmark for quantitative trading strategies multi-factor high-frequency performance evaluation risk-adjusted returns Sharpe Sortino VaR backtesting" search_time="2026年5月19日12时27分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>Deep Learning for Options Trading: An End-To-End Approach</title><summary>We introduce a novel approach to options trading strategies using a highly scalable and data-driven machine learning algorithm. In contrast to traditional approaches that often require specifications of underlying market dynamics or assumptions on an option pricing model, our models depart fundamentally from the need for these prerequisites, directly learning non-trivial mappings from market data to optimal trading signals. Backtesting on more than a decade of option contracts for equities listed on the S&P 100, we demonstrate that deep learning models trained according to our end-to-end approach exhibit significant improvements in risk-adjusted performance over existing rules-based trading strategies. We find that incorporating turnover regularization into the models leads to further performance enhancements at prohibitively high levels of transaction costs. Merton [25] regard options as redundant assets. While these approaches offer a tractable no-arbitrage pricing framework, they necessitate thorough specifications of underlying dynamics and require assumptions such as a frictionless market and the ability of market makers to perfectly hedge their exposures. Practically, these models are often vulnerable to model mispecification and are usually too simplistic to sufficiently account for empirically observed variations in option returns [6]. Recent works have challenged this framework, demonstrating that option prices have been influenced by additional risks beyond the underlying asset’s exposure [9, 13, 15], with several studies documenting the existence of mispricing in the options market [1, 12]. Despite the accelerating growth of the options market and the evidence of options mispricing, there is a surprising lack of research on a scalable machine learning-based strategy that is able to directly leverage the abundance of data to conduct options trading on behalf of an active investor. In this work, we address this gap by introducing a novel class of deep learning models capable of managing and trading a portfolio of options in a highly data-driven approach. Previous research has conventionally approached the complexities of managing portfolios of options by developing methods for optimal hedging and accurately pricing options. Our model departs fundamentally from the need for these prerequisites, and are directly optimized to learn highly non-trivial mappings from observed data to optimal trading decisions based on risk-adjusted performance. The resulting end-to-end framework does not depend on specific market dynamics, and can be extended broadly across instruments where market data is available. To illustrate our approach, we construct the framework by training end-to-end neural networks of different complexities and show that our models are able to outperform existing rules-based strategies in managing a portfolio of options, demonstrating strong risk-adjusted returns over a backtest period of over a decade. We subsequently extend our models to incorporate turnover regularization during optimization, leading to further performance enhancements in the presence of high transaction costs.</summary><hostname>arXiv</hostname><author_list><author name="Wee Ling Tan" affiliation="Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance, University of Oxford, Oxford, United Kingdom" /><author name="Stephen Roberts" affiliation="Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance, University of Oxford, Oxford, United Kingdom" /><author name="Stefan Zohren" affiliation="Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance, University of Oxford, Oxford, United Kingdom" /></author_list><url>https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2407.21791</url><publish_time>2024年7月31日0时0分</publish_time><arxiv_url>https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2407.21791</arxiv_url>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="comparative evaluation framework quantitative trading strategies benchmark multi-factor HFT performance risk adaptability market conditions" search_time="2026年5月19日12时27分星期二"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:6"><title>TradeMaster: A Holistic Quantitative Trading Platform Empowered by Reinforcement Learning</title><summary>The financial markets, which involve over $90 trillion market capitals, attract the attention of innumerable profit-seeking investors globally. Recent explosion of reinforcement learning in financial trading (RLFT) research has shown stellar performance on many quantitative trading tasks. However, it is still challenging to deploy reinforcement learning (RL) methods into real-world financial markets due to the highly composite nature of this domain, which entails design choices and interactions between components that collect financial data, conduct feature engineering, build market environments, make investment decisions, evaluate model behaviors and provides user interfaces. Despite the availability of abundant financial data and advanced RL techniques, a remarkable gap still exists between the potential and realized utilization of RL in financial trading. In particular, orchestrating an RLFT project lifecycle poses challenges in engineering (i.e., hard to build), benchmarking (i.e., hard to compare) and usability (i.e., hard to optimize, maintain and use). To overcome these challenges, we introduce TradeMaster, a holistic open-source RLFT platform that serves as a i) software toolkit, ii) empirical benchmark, and iii) user interface. Our ultimate goal is to provide infrastructures for transparent and reproducible RLFT research and facilitate their real-world deployment with industry impact. TradeMaster will be updated continuously and welcomes contributions from both RL and finance communities.</summary><hostname>NeurIPS Proceedings</hostname><publisher>37th Conference on Neural
